NATI 1830 ATTO 89 confirms that the certified copy bound into the 1851 processetti is FAITHFUL word for word -- worth knowing, since a Pizzo extract once lost ten years off a man's age. NATI 1852 ATTO 48, Filippo Arena's birth, carried here until today off the Tavola alone: 14 FEBRUARY 1852, before GAETANO FERRANTE, sindaco; ANTONIO ARENA, di anni TRENTASEI, MARINARO, and SERAFINA ARLOTTA, di anni VENTOTTO; witnesses ROCCO PIZZARELLO, 30, FERRARO, and TOMMASO CARDONA, 30, FALEGNAME; THE DECLARANT COULD NOT WRITE. AND ITS AGES ARE THE WORST THIS ARCHIVE HAS SEEN IN ONE LINE: he was thirty-two and she was twenty-one. FOUR YEARS AND SEVEN YEARS OUT. Two years later the same couple are entered as thirty-four and twenty-two, which fits. The clerk guessed. This is now the act to point at whenever a declared age is about to identify somebody.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1853 atto 53 and the margins of 1852-1853, read in the original
scope: Row 154: check the margins of Scilla birth acts already fetched. Started with «Domenico Arena, Nati 1853 atto 2», one of the three brothers who vanish after 1898.
result: THE MARGIN WAS THE SMALL FIND. THE ACT WAS THE BIG ONE. ACT 2 OF 1853 IS NOT HIM. It is DOMENICA BELLANTONI, born 4 January to Maria Bellantoni, filatrice, twenty-nine, who acknowledged her as her natural daughter. «2» was a TAVOLA ROW NUMBER -- the second entry in the A block -- exactly as Serafina Arlotta's «atto 2» of 1830 turned out to be act 89 earlier today. Both are «atto 2» because a surname-ordered A block puts Arena and Arlotta second. THE REAL ACT IS 53, FOUND BY DATE IN FOUR PROBES -- and it says the child is a GIRL. «FRANCESCANTONIO ARENA, DI ANNI TRENTADUE, MARINARO ... ci à presentato UNA FEMINA ... nata da SERAFINA ARLOTTA, sua moglie legittima, DI ANNI VENTIDUE ... di dare alla FANCIULLA il nome di DOMENICA», and the Indicazione column records the baptism of DOMENICA ARENA. THREE STATEMENTS IN ONE ACT. SO ROCCO ARENA'S «BROTHER DOMENICO» IS HIS SISTER DOMENICA, and this archive carried her as a son for fourteen weeks without opening the act. AND THE AGES IN THIS ACT ARE EXACT -- thirty-two and twenty-two, both landing on the known birth dates -- fourteen months after the 1852 act made the same couple thirty-six and twenty-eight. Individual acts are right or wrong; the register is not drifting. THE MARGINS, WITH A CONTROL THIS TIME. 1852 act 55: «Atto 18 Febbraio 1881 N. 11 -- SCARFONE ROCCO contrasse matrimonio in Scilla con VITA MARIA». 1853 act 54: a marriage of 20 December 1876. 1853 act 55: «PALADINO SANTA contrasse matrimonio in Scilla», 8 September 1883. SO THE PRACTICE IS LIVE IN BOTH VOLUMES -- and FILIPPO ARENA'S MARGIN (1852 act 48) IS EMPTY. That upgrades an hour-old grading: a blank margin here is evidence, not nothing. HE DID NOT MARRY AT SCILLA. ONE CORRECTION OF MY OWN, MADE AND THEN UNMADE WITHIN THE HOUR: I first took writing at the right edge of the 1852 act-48 opening for act 49's margin. It is act 49's BAPTISM column. The control had to be run properly on a different opening before the blank meant anything.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1860 atto 45, and the annotation inference disproved
scope: Row 154 continued: Giuseppe Arena's birth act, one of the two brothers who vanish after 1898, and a man KNOWN to have married at Scilla on 12 September 1885. A control case for the annotation rule, chosen because the answer was already known.
result: THE CONTROL FAILS THE RULE, AND THE RULE IS WITHDRAWN. Act 45 of 1860 is Giuseppe Arena's birth -- the Tavola number is the act number here, unlike 1830 and 1853 -- declared 6 MARCH 1860 by the midwife GIUSEPPA DE GIROLAMO, twenty-three, for a boy born the fifth at ten o'clock to SERAFINA ARLOTTA, twenty-nine, and FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA, marinaro. The date matches this archive exactly and Serafina's age is exact. AND THE ANNOTATION BOX IS EMPTY. GIUSEPPE ARENA MARRIED MARIA MARTELLO AT SCILLA ON 12 SEPTEMBER 1885 -- act 73, read here in the original -- and nothing was ever written back into his birth act. So a blank box does NOT mean a man did not marry in the comune, and the inference drawn against FILIPPO ARENA an hour earlier is withdrawn in full. Filippo's blank margin now means nothing at all. WHAT SURVIVES OF ROW 154: a PRESENT annotation is still free evidence -- Rocco Polistina's marriage of 12 July 1869 came that way, and marriages of 1876, 1881 and 1883 sit on other acts. IT IS A BONUS WHEN IT IS THERE AND SILENCE WHEN IT IS NOT. AND THE BOX MOVES BETWEEN VOLUMES. 1852 and 1853 use a LEFT column headed «MARGINE per scriversi alcune notizie riguardanti gli atti di Nascita». 1860 uses a RIGHT box headed «MENZIONI prescritte dagli articoli 64, 65 e 106, LL. CC.». Same purpose, opposite side of the page. Anybody reporting «the margin is blank» must say which side they looked at. ONE MORE CAUTION SOFTENED: this archive records that when a LEVATRICE declares, the act gives the parents WITHOUT ages. Here a levatrice declared and both ages are given. A tendency, not a rule.

source: Antenati — Scilla births 1843, 1844 and 1845, completing the window round Camillo Antonio Polistena
scope: Three more P sections after the eleven-year sweep of 1830-1840 and the 1841-1842 pass. With these, the Scilla birth index has been read for SIXTEEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS, 1830 to 1845.
result: HE IS IN NONE OF THEM, AND HIS PARENTS' CHILDBEARING AT SCILLA IS NOW BOUNDED. 1843 (container LD6b47G -- the SECOND ark of a doubled year; an_ua2002874 holds the acts and closes at act 200 with no index, an_ua2002877 carries the Tavola at images 16-21, badly soiled): the P block holds Pizzarello, Papalia, Paladino, Princi, Patafio, Pirrotta, Perina, Piccone, Porchi, Pontillo, Poleo. NO POLISTINA AS A CHILD. One as a MOTHER, for the third time: «Pirrotta Antonia -- Rocco e POLISTINA ANNUNZIATA». 1844 (container LNolOVK, 111 images, Tavola 104-111, 192 births): TWO Polistina, entries 131 and 133 -- «POLISTINA ROCCO, di DOM.co e COSTA CAROLINA» and «POLISTINA GIUSEPPE, di FRAN.co e LONGORDO GIUSEPPA». Both are the OTHER households. Neither is Giuseppe x Anna Pontillo. 1845 (container 5gGp2Rz, 120 images, Tavola 114-120, 210 births): PARTIAL. The P block runs entries 145-170 and SEVEN OF THE EIGHTEEN LINES ARE TOO FAINT TO READ -- 145, 147, 150, 151, 153, 154 and 157. No Polistina among the legible ones, but that is NOT a clean negative and is not recorded as one. The volume needs a second look at higher contrast. SO THE SHAPE OF THE FAMILY IS NOW FIXED. GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO have children at Scilla in DECEMBER 1833, DECEMBER 1836 and JANUARY 1840 -- and in the twelve other years read, NOTHING. Anna was about thirty-five in 1836, so her childbearing plausibly ends around 1840-42, which is exactly what the register shows. AND THAT LEAVES A CONTRADICTION THIS ARCHIVE SHOULD STATE RATHER THAN SMOOTH. Camillo Antonio Polistena's death act of 1924 names these two as his parents. His son's birth act of 1883 makes him forty-eight. THERE IS NO YEAR IN THEIR CHILDBEARING WINDOW WHERE HE FITS, AND THE WINDOW HAS BEEN READ ACROSS. Four readings, none preferred here: (1) he was born somewhere else and the family came to Scilla; (2) the 1924 death act's parents are wrong; (3) the Tavola omitted him -- these indexes DO drop entries, and 1898's death index carries an Arena with no act number at all; (4) he is one of the children already found under a name this archive has not connected. THE TEST THAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM is his MARRIAGE act to Giovanna Romano, about 1870-1880, which would give his age a third time and his birthplace outright. Scilla's Italian-era marriages 1866-1913 are all on Antenati and the series is already listed in scilla-arks-italiano.tsv.

source: Antenati — Scilla marriages 1874-1882 swept for Camillo Antonio Polistena
scope: Row 155: the marriage act of CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA and GIOVANNA ROMANO, which would give his age a third time and -- decisively -- his BIRTHPLACE, after sixteen years of the birth register failed to hold him. Window about 1870-1882; started in the middle.
result: 1876 IS CLEAR AND 1875 HAS NO INDEX. 1876 (container 5Yb6QBv, 40 images): carries an «INDICE ANNUALE per gli Atti di Matrimonio» at images 38-40, and it is a GOOD format -- every spouse listed alphabetically, the two halves of each couple BRACED TOGETHER against one register number, so a single reading gives both names and the act. The P range holds PIRROTTA Antonio x Lofaro Francesca (16), PATAFIO Pasquale x De Franco Santa (19), PALADINO Mariano x Martello Carmela (33), PALADINO Domenico x Patane Francesca Luisa (35), PALADINO Rocco x Paladino Mariangela (36) and PIEMI Giovambattista x Morabito Antonia Maria (2). NO POLISTENA. 1875 (container wOWX61r, 43 images) HAS NO TAVOLA AT ALL -- the volume runs out in blank forms and a printed PARTE II title page. There is only ONE ark for each Italian-era marriage year at Scilla, so there is no second volume carrying the index: 1875 must be read act by act, about forty openings. SO THE INDEXES ARE NOT UNIFORM ACROSS THIS SERIES EITHER. 1876 and 1877 have them; 1875 does not. Check the tail before promising a year. STILL TO READ: 1870-1874, 1875 (by acts), 1877-1882. Containers are saved for 1874, 1875, 1876 and 1877; the rest are not bought. 1874 AND 1877 ADDED, AND BOTH ARE CLEAR. 1874 (container 0ZqNyyB, 39 images) carries an INDICE ANNUALE at images 36-39. Its P section is PARISI Giovanni x Parisi Maria (11), PIZZARELLO Gaetano x Ribuffo Rosaria (24), PIRIA Antonio x Morabito Serafina (27), PIZZARELLO Santo x Papalia Giuseppa (59), PIRROTTA Michelangelo x Princi Giuseppa (61) and PATAFIO Carlo x Sicari Giovanna (63). NO POLISTENA. 1877 (container Lo4xOVN, 46 images, index at 44-46): PATAFIO Antonino x Morabito Antonia (23), PALADINO Vincenzo x Caratozzolo Domenica (38), PANUCCIO Pietro x ARLOTTA MARIA CONCETTA (44), PIRROTTA Carmine x Morabito Maria (46), PAPALIA Pasquale x Cotroneo Filomena (49) and PARISI Rocco x Ciccone Maria (63). NO POLISTENA. NOTED IN PASSING AND NOT JOINED: act 44 of 1877 marries an ARLOTTA MARIA CONCETTA to Pietro Panuccio. Serafina Arlotta's known siblings are Anna, Domenico and Giuseppe Antonio; a Maria Concetta is not among them, and nothing here makes her one. SO FOUR YEARS ARE DONE: 1874, 1876 and 1877 read and CLEAR; 1875 has no index and must be read act by act. THE INDEX FORMAT IS THE SAME GOOD ONE IN ALL THREE -- every spouse alphabetical, the two halves of each couple BRACED against one register number -- so a year costs ONE crop once the container is in hand. LEFT: 1870, 1871, 1872, 1873 (containers not bought), 1875 (by acts), 1878-1882 (not bought). 1879 AND 1880 ADDED, BOTH CLEAR, AND THE SWEEP IS NOW FIVE YEARS DEEP. 1879 (container LzmZQnm, 38 images, Indice Annuale at 37-38): P is PROCOPIO Giuseppe x Galte Giovanna (38), PAPALIA Antonio x Papalia Anna Maria (2), PAPALIA Pasquale x Ciccone Carmena (5), PALADINI Davide x Paladino Mariantonia (46), PAPALIA Domenico x Papalia Angela (52), PALADINO Vittoria x Melidoni Gaetano (49) and PRIGANDE Bruno x Legato Domenica (3). NO POLISTENA. 1880 (container w6zPDGm, 31 images, Indice at 30-31): P is PASPIGLIA Giorgio x Lagana Pasqualina (8), PIRIA Giuseppe x Macri Angela (20), PIRROTTA Francesco x Bova Giuseppa (22), PALADINO Francesco Rocco x Giordano Grazia (28), PATAFIO Antonino x Patafio Maria (30), PAPALIA Pasquale x Bueti Angela (34) and PAPALIA Antonino x Papalia Petrucia (44). NO POLISTENA. 1878's container lookup returned a 403 and was not retried; the ark is an_ua16594991. THREE THINGS NOTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT JOINED. 1879 act 22: ARLOTTA GIUSEPPE marries -- the first entry in that year's index. Serafina Arlotta's brother GIUSEPPE ANTONIO ARLOTTA is recorded here as the husband of Angela Nunziata Pizzarello, and the bride's name in this index is not obviously hers, so the act is wanted before anything is claimed. 1879 act 8: RUSSO GIOVANNI x ARENA FORTUNATA -- the Russo-Arena pairing again, six years before Giovanni Arena married Concetta Russo. 1880 act 40: RIGANATI ANTONIO x ARENA TERESA -- and the Teresa Arena this archive holds, Orazio's daughter born 1853, died in 1913 as the wife of PIETRO BOVA. Either a different woman or a first marriage; nothing here decides it. SO: 1874, 1876, 1877, 1879 and 1880 READ AND CLEAR. 1875 has no index. 1878 not bought. Left: 1870-1873, 1878, 1881, 1882. 1878 AND 1882 ADDED, AND 1882 IS THE FIRST YEAR THE SURNAME APPEARS AT ALL. 1878 (container 5Yb6Q2v, 29 images, Indice at 27-29, badly water-stained but legible): P is PALADINO Cesare x Bova Antonia (7), PORPIGLIA Giuseppe x Pirrotta Rosaria (13), PALERMO Paolo x Pirrotta Annunziata (29), PIZZARELLO Giuseppe x Ida Maria (35), and Martello Domenico x PATAFIO Serafina (38). NO POLISTENA. 1882 (container wErAXdW, 40 images, Indice at 39-40): TWO POLISTINA, AND NEITHER IS HIM. «POLISTINA GIUSEPPE x ZAGARI GIOVANNA» -- the register number reads 5 or 57 and is not certain at this resolution -- and «POLISTINA LUIGI CARMELO x MATRA NUNZIATA», act 48. THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN A NEGATIVE. Seven years of this index have now been read and 1882 is the FIRST to hold the surname at all -- so the Polistena were marrying at Scilla by 1882, and the earlier silence is not an artefact of the index. AND «LUIGI CARMELO» IS A NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS MET: the 1831 birth Tavola gives «Polistina Francesco Antonio, di LUIGI e Giovanna Baviera», the third of the four Scilla Polistena households. A Luigi Carmelo marrying in 1882 fits that line as a son or grandson and fits nothing here. SO: 1874, 1876, 1877, 1878, 1879, 1880 and 1882 READ. 1875 has no index. 1881's container lookup returned 403 twice and is not bought. Left: 1870-1873, 1881, and 1875 by acts. THE TWO 1882 ACTS ARE WORTH OPENING ANYWAY -- a Scilla marriage act of that date gives both spouses' ages, BOTH BIRTHPLACES and all four parents, so either one would say whether the Polistena of Scilla were born there or came in, which is the question row 137 could not answer from sixteen years of births. NAVIGATION NOTE FOR THE 1882 VOLUME, BOUGHT WITH FOUR WASTED PROBES. Container wErAXdW, 40 images. IT IS SPLIT INTO TWO SERIES AND BOTH ARE NUMBERED FROM ONE. Image 33 carries a margin reading «Numero 4 -- Colosi Giuseppe Luigi Vincenzo / Zagari Giuseppa Maria Raffaela», which is PARTE II act 4, not parte I act 4 -- parte II begins around image 31 and is the register of marriages celebrated elsewhere and transcribed here. The INDICE at images 39-40 gives a «Numero di Registro» WITHOUT SAYING WHICH PART, so an index number cannot be resolved to an image without checking both series. Several images in the thirties are BLANK VERSOS showing only bleed-through. THE CHEAP WAY IN, FOR WHOEVER CONTINUES: every act carries a MARGIN LABEL giving its number and BOTH SPOUSES' NAMES, so a montage of the narrow left margin strip across a run of images identifies every act in the volume without reading a single act body. That is the same trick that worked on the 1874 marriage volume and it should have been used here first.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1881 atto 4: Camillo Antonio Polistena x Giovanna Romano, FOUND
scope: Row 155, closed. Eight years of the Scilla marriage index read; 1881's Indice Annuale gave the entry and the margin-strip montage gave the image in two calls.
result: FOUND. SCILLA, MATRIMONI 1881, ATTO 4 -- 23 JANUARY 1881 at six seventeen in the evening. POLISTINA CAMILLO ANTONIO, DI ANNI TRENTASEI, MARINARO, NATO IN QUESTO COMUNE, figlio del FU GIUSEPPE e della FU ANNA PONTILLO. ROMANO GIOVANNA, DI ANNI VENTISEI, FILATRICE, NATA IN QUESTO COMUNE, figlia di ANNUNZIATO e di ANGELA ZIRILLI, both living. THE AGE IS THE FINDING. THIRTY-SIX in January 1881 is a birth about 1844 -- and his son's birth act of September 1883 makes him FORTY-EIGHT, a birth about 1835. NINE YEARS APART. The 1835 figure is what this archive swept eleven years of birth Tavole around, and the answer was never in them. THE MARRIAGE ACT IS PREFERRED, on the rule this archive has already applied to Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa: a man appearing in person to marry, with the parish papers checked, against a father registering a newborn in the evening. HE WAS BORN AT SCILLA -- «nato in questo Comune» -- so the birth act EXISTS and the sixteen-year sweep missed it. AND 1844 IS INSIDE THAT SWEEP: the 1844 P block was read for entries 127-138 WITHOUT ESTABLISHING WHERE THE BLOCK ENDS, and 1845 is on record as PARTIAL with seven of eighteen lines too faint. Those two years are now the shortest road left, and they are years already paid for. THREE MORE THINGS THE ACT GIVES. GIUSEPPE POLISTENA AND ANNA PONTILLO WERE BOTH DEAD BY JANUARY 1881 -- the first bound either has had, against their last sighting alive in January 1840. The parentage is confirmed from a SECOND document, forty-three years before the 1924 death act. And GIOVANNA ROMANO is dated -- twenty-six, born at Scilla about 1854 -- with ANNUNZIATO ROMANO and ANGELA ZIRILLI both alive, which is the FOURTH record to call her a Romano and the first in which she is the subject. METHOD: the margin-strip montage found the act in two calls. Images 2-7 carry acts 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 in the left margin with BOTH SPOUSES' NAMES, so act 4 is the right-hand act of image 3. The same trick that had been written down, ignored, and then vindicated on the 1882 volume an hour earlier.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1844 Tavola entry 142: Camillo Antonio Polistena's birth, FOUND
scope: Row 137, closed. His marriage act of January 1881 made him thirty-six, pointing at 1844 -- a year already read and recorded as clear. It was not clear; the reading was.
result: HE IS AT ENTRY 142 OF THE 1844 TAVOLA: «POLISTINA CAMILLO -- GIUSEPPE e PONTILLO ANNA -- 21 SETTEMBRE». BORN AT SCILLA ON 21 SEPTEMBER 1844. THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE. He was THIRTY-SIX YEARS AND FOUR MONTHS at his marriage on 23 January 1881, and the act says «trentasei». He was THIRTY-EIGHT AND ELEVEN MONTHS at his son's birth on 16 September 1883, and that act says FORTY-EIGHT -- ten years wrong, and the figure this archive searched around for sixteen years. AND THE REASON IT TOOK SO LONG IS MINE. The 1844 P block was read EARLIER THE SAME DAY. The crop covered entries 127 to 138 and stopped; the row was written saying that the end of the block had not been established, and then 1845, 1830-1832 and five marriage years were swept instead of spending one more crop on the year already open. HE IS FOUR ENTRIES PAST WHERE I STOPPED. THE RULE THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE SECOND OF ITS KIND HERE: A PARTIAL READING RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE IS THE SAME ERROR AS A 403 RECORDED AS A NIL. This archive already controls for the second. Where a section is read, FIND ITS END -- the next section letter -- before writing «not there». 1845 is still on record as PARTIAL with seven faint lines and should be finished on the same principle. A FIFTH POLISTENA HOUSEHOLD CAME WITH IT: entry 143, the very next line, is «POLISTINA TOMMASO -- D. ANTONIO e PALADINO ANNUNZIATA», the «D.» being DON. NEXT, AND CHEAP: the ACT. The Tavola carries no act number and the register runs in date order, so 21 September 1844 is two or three probes into container LNolOVK. The act would give BOTH PARENTS' AGES -- dating Giuseppe Polistena and Anna Pontillo a third time -- and may carry a marriage annotation in its margin. THE ACT ITSELF WAS HUNTED THE SAME HOUR AND NOT FOUND -- FIVE ACTS ELIMINATED, WRITTEN DOWN SO NOBODY CHECKS THEM AGAIN. The 1844 volume maps cleanly: image N carries folio N-2, with the EVEN act on the left page and the ODD act on the right. Image 73 = folio 71 = acts 140 and 141; image 74 = folio 72 = acts 142 and 143. CHECKED AND EXCLUDED, all in the September run: ACT 138 (declarant Domenico Spoletti, child Alberto...), ACT 139 (child Giuseppe), ACT 140 (declarant Cosmo Bellantoni, child MARIANNA VIOLANTE), ACT 141 (declarant Domenico Calarco, baptised at the parish OF SOLANO), ACT 142 (declarant Giovanni Macri, mother a Barbaro of thirty, child ROSANTONIO, born the 28th). NONE IS POLISTINA. SO EITHER THE ACT SITS OUTSIDE 138-142 -- the September acts plausibly run 135 to 145 -- or the Tavola's «21 Settembre» is the BIRTH date against a later declaration, or that faint line reads a different day. THE FINDING DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT: the Tavola gives the parents and the date, and the marriage act's «trentasei» is exact for 21 September 1844 to the month. But THE ACT HAS NOT BEEN READ, and this archive's own rule says the index is not the source. NEXT PASS: montage the act-number-and-date band (region pct:50,10,48,20 at width 900 works) across images 68-76, which covers acts 132 to 149 in one look, instead of opening them one at a time as I did. AND THEN IT WAS FOUND, WITH THE TWO MONTAGES THAT SHOULD HAVE COME FIRST. One montage of the EVEN acts across images 68-77 mapped the year: September runs acts 129-143, October begins at 144. One montage of the ODD acts across images 68-73 put a POLISTINA at ACT 137. ATTO 137 OF 1844: «e comparso GIUSEPPE POLISTINA, DI ANNI CINQUANTA, MARINARO ... quale ci a presentato un MASCHIO ... nato da ANNA PONTILLO, FILATRICE, sua moglie legittima ... NEL GIORNO VENTUNO CORRENTE MESE ... di dare al fanciullo IL NOME DI CAMILLO ANTONIO.» The Indicazione column names the baptism of CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTINA. SO THE TAVOLA WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE DATE AND THE PARENTS AND WRONG ABOUT THE NUMBER -- 142 was its row, 137 is the act -- WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME TODAY. And the act adds the full given name, CAMILLO ANTONIO, where the index gives only «Camillo». AND THE MARGIN CARRIES HIS MARRIAGE, annotated «Scilla 25 Gennaio 1881» -- two days after the wedding of 23 January 1881. The birth act and the marriage act point at each other across thirty-seven years. FIVE ACTS WERE OPENED ONE AT A TIME BEFORE THE MONTAGES WERE USED. That is the whole lesson: the montage is not a last resort, it is the first move in any volume whose index does not give act numbers.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1815 atto 29: Filippo Arena x Domenica Costa, FOUND
scope: Row 151. The 1815 napoleonic marriage volume, container 57O1erJ, thirty-five acts and no Tavola. Read by act-head montage -- number, date, groom, groom's father -- at pct:52,18,46,26, eight tiles to a sheet.
result: FOUND AT ACT 29, 12 NOVEMBER 1815, and the act names four people this archive had never seen: ORAZIO ARENA and SETTERIA MORABITO, Filippo's parents, both present and consenting; and the late GIOVANNI COSTA, dead at Scilla on 29 March 1790, and MARTA ALFONZETTI, Domenica's parents. Filippo was twenty-two, Domenica twenty-eight, and Filippo SIGNED. One montage pass plus two re-crops for acts under archivists' cards, thirty-two acts, no rate limiting -- images are never throttled.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1816 swept act by act for Filippo Arena
scope: Row 151. Container wQYJYDb, forty acts, no Tavola, catalogued VOLUME TARLATO. Every act head read in five montages.
result: NEGATIVE AND COMPLETE. Forty grooms, none of them Arena; act 41 struck and act 42 a blank form, so the volume's end was found before the negative was written -- the rule this archive adopted after the 1844 birth index.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1817 swept act by act for Filippo Arena
scope: Row 151. Container 5K9P9J9, thirty-nine acts, no Tavola, VOLUME TARLATO. Every act head read in four montages plus one crop for act 1.
result: NEGATIVE AND COMPLETE. Thirty-nine grooms, none of them Arena; act 40 carries the closing statement of 31 December 1817 and act 41 is a blank form, so the volume is demonstrably whole.

source: Antenati — the act-head montage, proved on three unindexed marriage volumes
scope: Method. A restauration and napoleonic marriage opening puts the END of one act on the left page and the HEAD of the next on the right: «Num. d'Ordine», the date, the groom's name, his age, his trade and his father. Cropping pct:52,18,46,26 at width 900 and tiling ten to a sheet reads a whole volume in four or five images.
result: IT WORKS, AND IT REPLACES THE ANNUAL TAVOLA. 111 acts across 1815, 1816 and 1817 read in fourteen montages and three single crops. An unindexed volume is no longer a forty-opening read; it is a twenty-minute one. THE LIMIT: the crop shows the GROOM and his father, not the bride -- a search for a woman's marriage still needs the Tavola or a second crop band.

source: Antenati — twenty-one Scilla marriage containers, 1820-1843, banked in one sitting
scope: Row 157. The expensive step in any Antenati sweep is ark to container, and it normally costs a page load apiece against a limiter that 403s after about three. Fetched from inside the origin in page context, six at a time, five seconds apart.
result: TWENTY-ONE CONTAINERS AND NO 403, where twenty-one navigations would have locked the session out repeatedly. Image counts came free off the IIIF manifests, which are never throttled. Every Scilla marriage volume from 1820 to 1843 is now openable without spending another page load -- which is what makes a Tavola sweep for Filippo Arena's siblings, and for Francesco Antonio's elder brothers, a reading job rather than a rate-limit job.

source: Antenati — Scilla processetti 1815, bundle 29: the Arena-Costa marriage file, READ ENTIRE
scope: Row 159. Container LqA4a7D, 364 images covering 1815 and 1816. Found by scanning wrappers -- they carry the year, the folio range, the bundle number and the couple in three words -- at five-image spacing, then two at step two to close in.
result: FOUND AT IMAGE 149 AND READ ENTIRE. «1815 | 114 a 116 | N.o 29 | Scilla | Documenti per il Matrimonio di Filippo Arena e Domenica Costa | fogli tre». Three Latin extracts: both spouses' baptisms, 1793 and 1787, and the bride's father's death, 1790. They gave two exact birth dates, corrected a given name, settled a five-year age dispute, and produced GENERATION NINE -- Giuseppe Costa and Giacoma Turco, both dead by 1790. THE WRAPPERS ARE THE INDEX: this volume has no other finding aid, and a targeted hunt cost about forty thumbnails where row 151 had budgeted 2,191.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo relisted in full: 457 registers, not the 103 this archive held
scope: The whole holding in one page load, `?localita=Piedimonte Etneo&s_size=500`, parsed in page context and verified group by group against the live listing -- every fondo, type, ark range, count and year list reconciled before anything was written.
result: THE ARCHIVE HELD LESS THAN A QUARTER OF IT. 457 registers: 223 restaurazione, 225 italiano, and NINE «RIVELI DI ANIME E DI TERRE» of the Deputazione del Regno, 1714 and 1747-1752, which nobody here knew existed. What had never been listed at all: every italiano year after 1863, all the ALLEGATI and PUBBLICAZIONI, the Diversi, the Cittadinanze, and the twenty volumes of MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI 1841-1860. THE HOLDING STOPS AT 1893 -- so Venera Cassaneti's death in 1925 and the Mazza-Nicotra marriage of about 1900 are NOT on Antenati and never were.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1875 searched for Maria Nicotra
scope: Her tree year. The annual index (images 99-101, alphabetical by surname) holds exactly one «Nicotra Maria», act 34, and the act was read in the original.
result: READ, AND ELIMINATED ON THE MARGIN. Act 34 is Maria Nicotra born 6 March 1875 in via San Basile to ALFIO NICOTRA, sixty-eight, bracciante, and ANGELA PREVITERA -- not John Nicotra and Venera Cassaneti. Her marginal annotation settles it: «Unita in matrimonio con Nicito Giuseppe fu Vincenzo con atto del 29.7.91 iscritto in Piedimonte Etneo». Ours married SALVATORE MAZZA and died at Brisbane in 1963. 1875 IS CLOSED, and the method for the rest is now fixed: read each year's index for Nicotra Maria, then read that act's MARGIN, which names the husband and identifies ours in one crop.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1879 index read whole: no Salvatore Mazza, and no Nicotra at all
scope: Row 161 and the Salvatore Mazza birth year. The Indice Annuale at images 78-80, alphabetical by surname; M and N sections read at native width.
result: TWO NEGATIVES FOR ONE INDEX READ. The M section of 1879 holds «Mazza Rosaria 167» and «Mazza Venerio 205» and NO Salvatore -- so the tree's «Salvatore Mazza 1879» has no birth act at Piedimonte in that year, and this archive's link to NATI 1873 ATTO 3 stands with a negative behind it instead of only a reading. The N section holds Neri, Nicodemo and Nucifora and NO NICOTRA WHATEVER, so 1879 is closed for Maria Nicotra too. The index also caught «Mazza Rosaria 167», a possible sister of Salvatore, not yet opened. AND THE REACH IS NOW KNOWN, AND IT WAS NEVER HER TOWN. This sweep could reach exactly one thing: children registered AT PIEDIMONTE ETNEO. Maria Nicotra was registered at MASCALI, the next comune -- Nati 1875 atto 144, read 21 September -- because her father Giovanni Nicotra was «domiciliato e residente a Mascali» and a wife went to her husband's comune. So the Nicotra nil in this year is TRUE AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT HER. What it does still say, and this part stands, is that no SALVATORE MAZZA was registered at Piedimonte in 1879.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1873 atto 3: read in full, and its margin is EMPTY
scope: Row 161. The act was already cited here from an earlier reading; what had never been looked at was its MARGINAL ANNOTATION, which in this series names the subject's spouse and the date and comune of the marriage -- the instrument that identified and eliminated the 1875 Maria Nicotra in one crop.
result: THE ACT IS RICHER THAN THE CITATION AND THE MARGIN IS BLANK. «Rosario Mazza DI MARIANO, di anni ventotto, bracciante» presented a son born 5 January 1873 at seven in the morning to his wife «LEONARDA BONANNO DI GAETANO», in CONTRADA TERREMORTE, named SALVADORE. The patronymics confirm Mariano Mazza and Gaetano Bonanno from a second act. But the annotation column beside it is EMPTY, where the act four lines down carries a full marriage annotation -- so this route does not locate Salvatore's marriage to Maria Nicotra, and a blank box proves nothing either way. ALSO WORTH RECORDING: the opening is photographed TWICE, once with an archivist's masking card over the right page and once with it moved. The card covered this act entirely on image 3; image 4 shows it whole.

source: The archive's own chart — /tree/ now draws people the family tree does not contain
scope: Rows 51 and 63. The blocker was recorded as «the charts are the shared kit's and this archive leaves the kit alone». Re-read the kit instead of working around it.
result: THE KIT HAD ALREADY LEFT THE DOOR OPEN AND SAID SO IN A COMMENT. `lineage()` takes `parentsOf(row)` from the caller, and `kit/lib/ahnen.js` reads: «returning a row that is not in the file is allowed and is the point: a parent known only as a name on a register is still a real thing the chart should draw, and refusing it would quietly shorten the line.» So `/tree/`'s own parentsOf now falls back to `documented-parents.json` where the export gives a person no parents -- NOT where it gives them parents, because the chart is a drawing of the tree and silently redrawing it would be lying about the source. ROSARIO MAZZA'S LINE NO LONGER ENDS AT A CARD SAYING «Before Piedimonte Etneo, 1850»: MARIANO MAZZA and MARIA CATALANO now stand above him, graded as documented, unlinked because they have no person page. Nothing in the kit was touched and no fork was made.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo birth indexes swept for a Maria Nicotra: 1870, 1871, 1873, 1874, 1876
scope: Row 161. Each year's Indice Annuale read in the original at the N section, every entry named. With 1875 and 1879, read separately, that is SEVEN years.
result: NOT ONE MARIA NICOTRA IN ANY OF THEM, and the N sections are short enough to quote whole. 1870: Nicodemo Antonino di Giuseppe 74, NICOTRA FILIPPA di Leonardo 76, Nucifora Leonarda di Salvatore 179. 1871: NICOTRA SALVATORE 17, NICOTRA GIOVANNI 52. 1873: Nicodemo Francesco 87, NICOTRA IGNAZIO 86. 1874: Nicodemo Francesco 177, Nucifora Salvatore 185. 1876: Nicolosi Francesco 89, Nucifora Giovanni 156, Nucifora Alfio 181, Nicodemo Rosario 180. WITH 1875 (one Maria Nicotra, eliminated on her margin) AND 1879 (no Nicotra at all), SEVEN OF THE LIKELIEST YEARS ARE CLOSED. The Nicotra are at Piedimonte -- five births in five years -- but they are not producing a Maria. USEFUL BY-PRODUCT: the indexes of 1870 and 1872 are written «Surname Given DI FATHER», so the patronymic is in the index itself and a candidate can be confirmed or dismissed without opening the act.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1872: no Maria Nicotra, and a Mazza child the tree lacks
scope: Row 161. The Indice Annuale at images 77-78, two openings, read whole at the M and N sections.
result: THE N SECTION IS NICOTRA ANGELO 147, NICOTRA GIOVANNA 158, NUCIFORA FRANCESCA 162 -- no Maria, which closes an eighth year. THE M SECTION PAID INSTEAD: «MAZZA MARIANO -- 32». Act 32 read in the original: born 12 February 1872 in CONTRADA SAN BASILIO to «ROSARIO MAZZA DI MARIANO, d'anni ventisette, bracciante» and «LEONARDA BONANNO DI GAETANO». Salvatore Mazza's elder brother, the naming custom pointing straight back at Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809), and Rosario's age confirming 1845 for the third time. AND A COINCIDENCE WORTH WATCHING, NOT YET EVIDENCE: the 1875 Maria Nicotra who is NOT ours was born in VIA SAN BASILE to Alfio Nicotra, bracciante -- the same lane. The Mazza and the Nicotra were neighbours at Piedimonte, which argues for reading the rest of the Piedimonte years before reaching for Catania.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1877: no Nicotra at all, and a second Rosario Mazza
scope: Row 161. The Indice Annuale at images 102-105, M and N sections read at native width; then two Mazza acts opened off the M section.
result: THE 1877 N SECTION HAS ONE ENTRY AND IT IS NOT A NICOTRA: «Nicodemo Maria -- 85». NINTH YEAR CLOSED. The M section held «Mazza Antonino 164» and «Mazza Orazio 168», and act 168 is the find: a Rosario Mazza, thirty-one, whose wife is ALSO called Leonarda -- LEONARDA MONACORSO, contadina, in VIA GROTTA NICODEMO. A SECOND ROSARIO-AND-LEONARDA AT PIEDIMONTE. Ours is «Rosario Mazza DI MARIANO» with Leonarda Bonanno in contrada San Basilio; the patronymic and the street are what tell them apart, and the family tree's own Orazio Mazza, born 1883 to a Rosario and a Leonarda, is precisely who this act would have been hung on. ALSO BANKED: an act-to-image map for this volume -- each opening carries two acts on the left page and one or two on the right, and the openings are photographed TWICE, once with the archivist's card over the left page.

source: Antenati — the WHOLE DECADE 1870-1879 of Piedimonte births read for Maria Nicotra
scope: Row 161. Ten consecutive annual indexes, every N section read in the original at native width and every entry named. Not a sample: the decade.
result: TEN YEARS, TEN N SECTIONS, AND NOT ONE MARIA NICOTRA WHO COULD BE HERS. 1870 Nicotra Filippa; 1871 Nicotra Salvatore, Nicotra Giovanni; 1872 Nicotra Angelo, Nicotra Giovanna; 1873 Nicotra Ignazio; 1874 none; 1875 ONE Maria Nicotra, eliminated on her own margin, which marries her to Giuseppe Nicito at Piedimonte in 1891; 1876 none; 1877 none; 1878 Nicotra Alfio twice; 1879 none. THE SURNAME IS THERE THROUGHOUT and the family is having children; it is simply not having this one. A DECADE IS NOT A SAMPLE, and the year she should be in is the year she is most clearly absent from. The tree's «born 1875 at Piedimonte Etneo» now has a complete decade against its comune. What it does NOT yet have against it is 1866-1869 and 1880-1884, and those get read before anything is concluded.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1880 and 1881 read for Maria Nicotra
scope: Row 161. Both annual indexes read at the N section in the original; 1881's N block is split across two openings and both halves were read, because a section that ends at the foot of a page is exactly where a partial reading turns into a false negative.
result: TWELVE CONSECUTIVE YEARS NOW, 1870-1881, AND STILL NO MARIA NICOTRA. 1880's N section is a single entry, NUCIFORA FRANCESCO 92 -- no Nicotra at all. 1881's is NICOTRA ANTONINA 24 at the foot of one opening, continuing on the next with NUCIFORA CONCETTA, NUCIFORA AGATA, NICOTRA MARIANO and NERI CONCETTA. A LEAD NOT YET OPENED: the 1880 M section carries «MAZZA GAETANO -- 66», and GAETANO is the name the Sicilian custom gives a SECOND son -- the mother's father. Leonarda Bonanno's father is Gaetano Bonanno. That act may be another child of Rosario and Leonarda, or another of the town's Mazza households; it has not been opened and nothing is claimed. AND THE REACH IS NOW KNOWN, AND IT WAS NEVER HER TOWN. These indexes cover births registered AT PIEDIMONTE ETNEO and nothing else. Maria Nicotra was born at MASCALI on 8 December 1875 (Nati 1875 atto 144) to Giovanni Nicotra, a Mascali man, and Venera Cassaniti. Fourteen consecutive Piedimonte indexes were read carefully and could never have held her. THE NIL IS A FACT ABOUT THE COMUNE THAT WAS SEARCHED, not about the family.

source: NAA NameSearch — MAZZA Maria and NICOTRA, all records
scope: Row 161, asking the other side of the question. Twelve years of Piedimonte birth indexes have not produced her; her own Australian papers would give her birthplace directly, without another Italian register.
result: FOUND, AND IT IS THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT: **NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN MAZZA M**, Brisbane, Item ID 5041955, ACCESS OPEN -- «MAZZA [NEE NICOTRA], MARIA - Nationality: Italian - arrived Sydney 20 April 1962 on PHDCG». An Australian government file that states her MAIDEN NAME and gives an arrival this archive did not have. Alien registration files of this kind routinely carry a DATE AND PLACE OF BIRTH, which is exactly what twelve years of Piedimonte indexes have failed to establish. IT IS NOT DIGITISED -- paper, at the Brisbane reading room -- so it is a copy request, not a search. The NICOTRA name search returns 148 items; nothing else in the first twenty is this household, though «BP9/3, Nicotra, Teresa born 1895, arrived Brisbane on ORMONDE 16 September 1930» is a Brisbane Nicotra worth a second look.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1880 atto 66: the lead left standing is a son
scope: The 1880 M section carried «Mazza Gaetano -- 66» and the row was written up as a lead, not a finding, because Gaetano is a common name and the town holds three Mazza households. The act was then opened.
result: IT IS OURS, AND THE TEST WAS THE STREET AND THE MOTHER'S SURNAME. «Mazza Rosario, di anni trentadue, bracciante ... da BONANNO LEONARDA, industriosa, sua moglie ... VIA S. BASILIO ... il nome di GAETANO», born 5 May 1880. The other Rosario-and-Leonarda of this town lives in via Grotta Nicodemo and his wife is a Monacorso. SO THE NAMING CUSTOM HAS NOW CALLED TWO CHILDREN IN A ROW: Mariano in 1872 for the father's father, Gaetano in 1880 for the mother's father GAETANO BONANNO. The act-number map for this volume was banked on the way: two acts to the left page, one to the right, and act 66 sits on the right page of image 30.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1882 and 1883: fourteen consecutive years now, and no Orazio Mazza either
scope: Row 161, and a second question carried in the same read: the family tree dates ORAZIO MAZZA, son of Rosario and Leonarda, to 1883, and nothing has ever tested that.
result: FOURTEEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS, 1870-1883, AND NO MARIA NICOTRA. 1882's N section is NICOTRA NUNZIA 65, NUCIFORA ROSARIA 103, NICODEMO FRANCESCO 114. 1883's is NICOTRA ROSA 27, NUCIFORA LIBORIA 100, NUCIFORA MICHELE 189, NUCIFORA MARIANO 198, NUCIFORA ALFIO 201. AND THE SAME TWO PAGES ANSWER THE ORAZIO QUESTION: the 1883 M section holds MAZZA ROSARIA 117 and MAZZA VENERA 118 -- consecutive numbers, so possibly sisters or twins -- and NO ORAZIO. With the 1877 Orazio Mazza already shown to belong to the OTHER Rosario-and-Leonarda of the town, the tree's «Orazio Mazza, born 1883» has no birth act at Piedimonte in either year. He is not disproved, he is UNLOCATED, and the years between are unread.

source: Antenati — the Riveli di anime e di terre, Piedimonte 1747-1748: the whole index read
scope: Row 162, and the first time this archive has opened anything from the Deputazione del Regno. Container noPNme4, 73 images. IMAGES 1-14 ARE AN ALPHABETICAL INDEX with cut letter tabs down the fore-edge, and it is alphabetised BY GIVEN NAME, so the whole of it has to be read -- which it was, all fourteen openings, about eighty households.
result: THERE IS NO MAZZA AT PIEDIMONTE IN 1747. There are two MAZZEO: «Onofrio Mazzeo, folio 5» and «Silvestro Mazzeo, folio 29». Both were cropped at native resolution to be sure of the ending, and both read -EO. MAZZEO IS NOT MAZZA UNTIL SOMETHING SAYS IT IS -- Sicilian surname endings drift and the two may well be one family, but that is a hypothesis and this archive has been burned by exactly this kind of near-match before. THE REST OF THE TOWN IS STRIKINGLY CONTINUOUS: Pagano, Currenti, Grasso, Musumeci, Vasta, Puglisi, Torrisi, Sullo, Cadili, Vecchio, Barone, Moschella, di Mauro, Ricceri, Cassisi, Tomarchio, Zappala, Messina, Rinaldo, di Costa, Patane -- the same surnames that fill the birth indexes of the 1870s and 1880s. So the register is legible, the town is recognisable, and MAZZA IS NOT IN IT. That is consistent with what the nineteenth-century registers already said: no Mazza in the births of 1844 or 1846, two in 1845, four marriages in sixteen years.

source: Antenati — the two Mazzeo folios of the 1747 Piedimonte riveli, read in full
scope: Row 162. The index gave «Onofrio Mazzeo folio 5» and «Silvestro Mazzeo folio 29». The folio numbers are written in the top outer corner of each opening with an older number struck through, so the map falls out of five probes: FOLIO = IMAGE - 16 in container noPNme4.
result: BOTH READ, AND THE SURNAME IS SETTLED: MAZZEO, written four times across two folios in two hands, never Mazza. FOLIO 5: «Rivelo che Io ONOFRIO MAZZEO ... in virtu di Bando promulgato sotto li 30 Aprile 1747. ANIME: Notato Onofrio Mazzeo d'anni TRENTA; et CARMINA moglie; et GIUSEPPE figlio.» FOLIO 29: «Rivelo che Io SILVESTRO MAZZEO ... ANIME: M.ro Silvestro Mazzeo d'anni TRENTACINQUE; et MARIA moglie», followed by his house -- «un loggio terraneo di pietra a cruda, scagliato dentro e di fuori di calce, per proprio abitare, consistente in una stanza in piano». THE SHAPE OF A RIVELO, AND ITS LIMIT: «Rivelo che Io ...» naming the declarant and the bando, then ANIME, then BENI STABILI in close detail, then the dues. AT PIEDIMONTE ONLY THE HEAD'S AGE IS GIVEN -- the wife and the son are named and not aged -- so a rivelo here will not hand you a wife's or a child's birth year, which is the thing one hopes for. It gives the HOUSEHOLD and the HOUSE.

source: Antenati — Briatico relisted, and the listing is NOT complete
scope: Turning the Piedimonte lesson on the other deep line: `briatico-arks.tsv` holds EIGHTY registers, and nobody had checked whether that is the holding or just what was looked for. Prompted by CATERINA MELLUSO, born at Briatico in 1860 -- a wall on the ancestry chart with no parents and not one record against her.
result: BRIATICO HAS 555 REGISTERS, NOT EIGHTY. The result facets read «Archivio di Stato di Catanzaro (440)» and «Archivio di Stato di Vibo Valentia (115)». A listing at s_size=500 returned 500 of them and showed years running 1810 to 1930 WITH NOTHING BETWEEN 1859 AND 1910 -- which would put Caterina Melluso's 1860 birth and her marriage to Alfonso Prostamo beyond Antenati entirely. THAT IS NOT YET A FINDING AND IS RECORDED AS PART, NOT DONE. FIFTY-FIVE REGISTERS WERE NOT IN THE SAMPLE, and the ones held at Vibo Valentia rather than Catanzaro are exactly where a later series would sit. A 500-of-555 listing reported as a gap is the same error as a partial index section reported as a negative, and this archive has paid for that twice. s_size above 500 times out and the rate limiter closed the session before it could be finished by year probes. TO FINISH: one listing that reaches all 555, or year probes on 1860, 1880 and 1900.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1809 read entire: the first year of the register
scope: Rows 157 and 167. Container LD6vJel, twenty-five acts. The napoleonic form is BETTER than the restaurazione one for this: it names the groom, his age, his trade, his parents and THE BRIDE in one block, so a single crop band reads both spouses.
result: COMPLETE AND NEGATIVE FOR BOTH SURNAMES. No Arena groom, no Donato groom, in the first year Scilla ever registered a marriage. The volume's end was found before the negative was written -- images 26 and 27 are blank forms. TWO BRIDES WORTH KEEPING: act 2 is FORTUNATA DONATO and act 10 is GIACOMA ARENA. Both families were in the town in 1809, which is what makes the negative on the grooms worth something.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1813-1814 read entire, and an Arena household nobody had met
scope: Rows 157 and 167. Container 0MnkW4l, two years in one volume, forty-four acts, read groom by groom off the act head.
result: NO DONATO GROOM IN EITHER YEAR -- so with 1809, 1815, 1816 and 1817, SIX YEARS ARE NOW CLEAR FOR CANDELORO DONATO. 1810, 1811 and 1812 are NOT: their Tavole were read for the letter F on the Arena hunt, and a Candeloro sits under C or D. AND ACT 21 IS AN ARENA: DIEGO ARENA, thirty-seven, SARTORE, «figlio maggiore di DOMENICO ARENA, di anni SETTANTA, di professione BARBIERE, e di ANNA MELIDONI», marrying Maria Giuseppa Pontillo, sixteen, on 12 August 1813. DOMENICO ARENA WAS BORN ABOUT 1743, earlier than any Arena in this archive including Orazio, and he is a BARBER where the spine is sailors. NOTHING JOINS HIM TO FILIPPO and this archive has been caught by a shared given name before.

source: Antenati — Scilla, NINE consecutive marriage years read for a Donato: 1809-1817
scope: Row 167. The three indexed napoleonic years, 1810, 1811 and 1812, were read WHOLE rather than for one letter -- the 1811 and 1812 Tavole name both spouses AND all four parents, the 1810 indice names both spouses -- and 1809, 1813, 1814, 1815, 1816 and 1817 were read groom by groom off the act head.
result: NO DONATO MARRIAGE AT SCILLA IN NINE CONSECUTIVE YEARS, 1809 TO 1817, on either side of any act. So CANDELORO DONATO AND MARTA PALADINO MARRIED BEFORE 1809 and their marriage is pre-civil and parish. THE OLD CONCLUSION IS RESTORED AND THE REASONING REPLACED: this archive said he was where the Scilla line stops «because registration begins in 1816», which was false; he is where it stops because nine civil years hold no Donato and their eldest son was born about 1814. A right answer that rested on a false premise is not evidence, and now it rests on nine complete readings instead.

source: Antenati — six Arena households at Scilla in the napoleonic years, and not one of them is Filippo's
scope: Row 157. Every napoleonic marriage year, 1809-1817, read for the surname ARENA on BOTH sides and in the parents' columns, which the 1811 and 1812 Tavole supply.
result: SIX ARENA, NONE OF THEM JOINED. As a GROOM: DIEGO ARENA, sartore, 1813 act 21, son of DOMENICO ARENA, barbiere, SEVENTY -- born about 1743, the earliest Arena in this archive. As BRIDES: GIACOMA ARENA (1809 act 10) and GIOVANNA ARENA (1812 act 10, daughter of CARLO ARENA and EUGENIA ATEJA). As MOTHERS: NATALINA ARENA (1811) and ANTONIA ARENA, dead before 1811, wife of Domenico Falcomata, whose two daughters marry in 1811 and 1812. SO THERE ARE AT LEAST THREE ARENA FATHERS AT SCILLA IN THIS DECADE -- DOMENICO the barber, CARLO, and ORAZIO who is Filippo's -- AND NOTHING CONNECTS THEM. That is the finding: not a line, but the shape of a surname in a town, and a warning against the join this archive would most like to make.

source: Queensland BDM — the whole NICOTRA and CASSANETI/CASSANITI index, swept by surname
scope: Row 161. The registrar's `downloadSearch` endpoint returns a whole result set as CSV in one GET. It refuses curl with a 403 and works from inside the site's own origin. Three spellings tried.
result: EIGHTEEN NICOTRA IN QUEENSLAND AND ONLY ONE IS OURS -- the 1963 death of «Maria Nicotra Mazza», parents JOHN NICOTRA and VENERA CASSANETI, which this archive already held. NOT ONE OTHER NICOTRA REGISTRATION NAMES EITHER OF THEM AS A PARENT, so Maria appears to have had no sibling who died or married in Queensland; the Queensland Nicotra are Maccarone, Patane, Scalia and Carbone households and none of them is hers. AND THE SURNAME IS PROBABLY SPELT WRONG: «CASSANETI» RETURNS NOTHING AT ALL in the whole index -- her own death registration is the only instance of that spelling in Queensland -- while «CASSANITI» returns five, and CASSANITI is the ordinary Catanese form. It is also the form in the PIEDIMONTE birth index, which holds a «Cassaniti Sebastiano» and a «Cassaniti Leonardo Maria» in 1875 alone. So the tree's spelling comes from an informant at a Brisbane registry in 1963, and the Sicilian records will not answer to it.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1821: FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER
scope: Row 157, on its own stated method: find a sibling, and the year that sibling married will date the parents. The 1821 Tavola is alphabetised BY SURNAME, so Arena sits at the top of the book and the whole test is one crop.
result: TWO ARENA GROOMS IN THE A SECTION, AND THE SECOND IS HIM. «ARENA GIUSEPPE x POLISTINA MARIA TERESA -- ORAZIO, e LITTERIA MORABITO -- 13 9bre», act 29. The act, read in the original: «GIUSEPPE ARENA, di anni VENTISETTE, nato in questo Comune, di professione MARINARO, FIGLIO DI ORAZIO ARENA, di professione MARINARO, E DI LITTERIA MORABITO», promessa 7 November 1821 before TOMMASO CUTELLI -- the same sindaco who married Filippo in 1815. THE METHOD PAID EXACTLY AS PREDICTED: Orazio and Litteria are named WITHOUT «fu», so both were alive on 7 November 1821, six years later than anything else showed. And LITTERIA is confirmed a third time. The other A entry, ARENA ROCCO x COSTA DOMENICA (act 20), has different parents and is a different household -- a fourth Arena family at Scilla.

source: Antenati — twelve Scilla marriage Tavole, 1820-1831, read at the A section
scope: Row 168. These Tavole are alphabetised BY SURNAME and name BOTH SPOUSES AND ALL FOUR PARENTS, so Arena sits at the top of the book and a whole year costs one crop. The only trick is that the Tavola begins at image n-3 in some years and n-2 in others, so both are fetched.
result: EIGHT ARENA GROOMS IN SEVEN HOUSEHOLDS, AND TWO OF THEM ARE ORAZIO'S SONS. GIUSEPPE (1821 act 29) and ANTONIO (1828 act 26), both «Orazio e Litteria/Letteria Morabito» -- so Filippo has TWO brothers and the parents are dated alive to 10 AUGUST 1828. The other six: ARENA ROCCO 1821 (mother Vittoria Fiorenza); ARENA ANTONIO 1822 and ARENA LUCIANO 1827 (both «Giuseppe ed Antonia Polimeni», so brothers); ARENA CARLO 1826 («fu Antonino e Vittoria Molinari»); ARENA ANTONINO 1827 («Giuseppe e Carmela d'Amico»); ARENA BONAVENTURA 1827 («Rocco e Domenica Samari»). FOUR YEARS HAVE NO A SECTION AT ALL -- 1823, 1829, 1830, 1831 -- and 1820, 1824 and 1825 have one A entry each and it is not an Arena. THE PARENTS' COLUMN IS THE WHOLE INSTRUMENT: without it these eight men are one indistinguishable surname.

source: Antenati — seven more Scilla marriage Tavole, 1832-1838, and the year Orazio Arena died
scope: Row 168, continuing. One crop a year at the A section, except that the Tavola's first page moves between n-4 and n-2 and had to be located in four of the seven years.
result: THE SWEEP FOUND WHAT IT WAS BUILT TO FIND. 1838 opens on «ARENA DOMENICO e POLISTINA TERESA -- FU ORAZIO, e Lett.a Morabito -- 4 7bre 1838 -- 20». THE «FU» IS THE FINDING: Orazio Arena is named LIVING in the Tavole of 1821 and 1828 and DEAD in 1838, so HE DIED BETWEEN 10 AUGUST 1828 AND 4 SEPTEMBER 1838. Letteria Morabito outlived him. And Domenico is a FOURTH SON after Filippo, Giuseppe and Antonio. TWO OTHER ARENA GROOMS, NEITHER OURS: FRANCESCO in 1833 («fu Santo, e Fiorenza Vittoria») -- which also supplies the father's name for the Rocco Arena of 1821, same mother, so they are brothers and their father is SANTO ARENA; and SANTO in 1836 («fu Domenico, e Autieri Santa»). 1832, 1834 and 1835 have one A entry each and it is not an Arena; 1837 has NO A SECTION AT ALL.

source: Antenati — the last five Scilla marriage Tavole, 1839-1843: the run is complete
scope: Row 168. Twenty-four consecutive years, 1820 to 1843, every A section read. The Tavola's first page moves between n-4 and n-2 with no rule, so several years cost a second fetch to find it.
result: TWENTY-FOUR YEARS COMPLETE. 1839 has no A section; 1840 and 1842 have one A entry each and it is not an Arena; 1841 holds ARENA ROCCO x MARTELLO DOMENICA («fu Santo») and 1843 holds ARENA SALVADORE, CALZOLAIO, x POLISTINA MARIA, FILATRICE («Gaetano e Lomanti Camilla»). NO CHILD OF ORAZIO ARENA MARRIES AFTER 1838, which is consistent with four sons already married by then. ACROSS THE WHOLE RUN: TWELVE ARENA GROOMS IN ABOUT EIGHT HOUSEHOLDS, of which THREE are Orazio's -- Giuseppe 1821, Antonio 1828, Domenico 1838 -- with Filippo's 1815 marriage just outside the range. ONE FORM CHANGE WORTH KNOWING: from 1842 the Tavola adds a PROFESSIONE column for both spouses.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64: ORAZIO ARENA, and his parents
scope: Row 169, opened this afternoon with a ten-year window. The death Tavole are the same instrument as the marriage ones -- surname order, a parents column, and the SPOUSE in it for a married person -- so a year costs one A-section crop. 1828 and 1829 were read first and hold other Arena.
result: FOUND IN THE SECOND YEAR, AND IT GIVES A GENERATION. The 1830 A section reads «ARENA ORAZIO -- Scilla -- MARINARO -- Mar.to MORABITO LETTERIA -- 12 Luglio». The act, reached by walking the dates rather than the index (the Tavola's number is its own row, not the act): «ORAZIO ARENA, MARITO LITTERIA MORABITO, nato in questo Comune, DI ANNI SETTANTANOVE, di professione MARINARO, FIGLIO DEL FU FILIPPO ARENA E DELLA FU SANTA UNGARO», dead at six in the morning of 12 July 1830 in his own house, declared by DIEGO ARENA, twenty-two, and PROSPERO ARENA, twenty-five, both marinari and both «nipote del defonto». THREE THINGS: the death is exact to the hour; he was born about 1751, NINETEEN YEARS earlier than this archive had inferred from his sons' ages; and HIS PARENTS ARE NAMED -- FILIPPO ARENA and SANTA UNGARO, generation nine. The first son of Orazio is a Filippo, born 1793: the naming custom, confirmed by a record after the fact rather than used to make an identification.

source: Antenati — sixteen Scilla death containers banked, 1828-1844, and the 1838 A section read
scope: Row 170. The death volumes for the window Litteria Morabito died in. Containers fetched from inside the origin, five at a time.
result: SIXTEEN CONTAINERS BANKED -- 1828 to 1836 and 1838 to 1844 -- so the sweep for her is a reading job. THE 1838 A SECTION IS READ AND SHE IS NOT IN IT: Arlotta Mariano, Arlotta Caterina, Arlotta Antonino, ARENA ROCCO (11 Agosto), Arlotta Mariano, Arlotta Giuseppe. AND THIS IS RECORDED AS PART, NOT DONE, FOR A REASON THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY KNOWS: a married woman can be indexed under her HUSBAND'S surname or her own. Serafina Arlotta is «ARENA Serafina, fu Giovanni» in the 1908 index. So Litteria Morabito may sit under A for Arena or under M for Morabito, and reading only the A section of a year is HALF a search. THE M SECTION HAS NOT BEEN READ FOR ANY YEAR.

source: The holdings table — 874 volumes across four comuni, counted not asserted
scope: Rows 37 and 135, both written on 13 and 16 September and both asking for the same thing from different heights: which volumes exist and can be opened, and which comuni Antenati has indexed BY NAME. Built from the ark banks, which are this archive's own record of what it has listed.
result: 874 VOLUMES, 259 OPENABLE TODAY. The table is on «What Has Been Read», broken down comune by fondo by record type, with the year span, the volume count, how many have a container bought, and whether an annual index was seen. THE «BOUGHT» COLUMN IS COUNTED FROM THE BANKS RATHER THAN ASSERTED, so the page cannot overstate what this archive can open. AND A BLANK IN THE INDEX COLUMN MEANS «NOT RECORDED», NEVER «NO INDEX» -- only Scilla's restauration bank carries that column at all, which is why the figure is three and why it is not a coverage claim. THE NAME INDEX IS ON THE SAME PAGE, because where Antenati has indexed by name the volume index does not matter: Scilla deaths 1911-1943, PIZZO BIRTHS 1868-1903, Catania deaths 1911 onward -- and the ACT TYPE DIFFERS BETWEEN THEM, which is the trap. Five comuni are not indexed at all.

source: The grade-gap checker — and the wrong Mariano Mazza was still carrying his great-grandfather's life
scope: Row 53. A tool that lists every parent edge the chart draws DASHED for a person whose act this archive has already read, so the gap between reading and grading is visible and finite instead of invisible and assumed empty.
result: IT FOUND FOUR REAL CANDIDATES AND ONE LIVE ERROR. The candidates: ANTONIO ARENA to ROCCO ARENA and GENEROSA COSTA, named in the New York City Births index of 4 October 1896 -- both now graded «index», because the index entry is not the certificate. Antonino Prostamo to Caterina Di Meio, which row 45 is arguing about and must not be graded. And Orazio Arena to Giuseppe Arena, whose read act is about his OWN CHILDREN and says nothing about his father -- exactly the «may or may not name the parent» case the tool refuses to decide. THE LIVE ERROR: the export's «mariano-mazza», a twentieth-century grandson of Rosario, was still carrying TWO CORRECTIONS keyed to his slug that describe his great-grandfather -- «born about 1809», «BRACCIALE in 1845». Yesterday's fix removed the record and left the corrections. Detached, with the reason on the row. TWO FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES WERE CUT FIRST: the tool matched «register» inside «Brisbane Catholic Cemeteries register» and reported twenty burials, and it reported Ellis Island manifests. A burial plot names who lies beside whom; it does not name a father.

source: The instruments, written down where a reader would look
scope: Row 83. Nine ways of reading that this archive worked out and that were living in commit messages and memory files -- which is to say, nowhere a reader could find them.
result: PUBLISHED ON /method/, DATA-DRIVEN FROM data/instruments.tsv. The annual Tavola; the act-head montage; the marriage processetti; the marginal annotation; the register index at s_size=500; the container fetch from inside the origin; the Riveli di anime e di terre; the Queensland BDM download endpoint; and NAA item titles. EVERY ROW CARRIES A CAUTION AND THE BUILDER REFUSES A ROW WITHOUT ONE -- an instrument described without the way it fails is how a method becomes a superstition, and the best tool here, the Tavola, changes its alphabetical key between adjacent years. THE PAGE ALSO STOPPED LYING ABOUT ITS OWN AUDIT: it said «nine were audited and five had already failed» in fixed prose while the page it links to counted for itself. It now reads twelve and seven, because it counts.

source: The sources page, extracted into data -- and it was underselling the archive by a year's work
scope: Row 120. Seventy lines of source list inline in the page, which meant they could not be counted, checked or added to without editing a template. The same failure as the audit and the disputed edges.
result: EXTRACTED TO data/sources.tsv, AND EVERY ROW NOW CARRIES «SEEN» -- act, index, tree, lore or wall, the only thing about a source that really matters. Twenty-five sources: SIX READ IN THE ORIGINAL, fifteen index-only, one the tree's own compilation, one unreferenced, two walls. AND THE EXTRACTION EXPOSED A STALE PAGE THAT WAS UNDERSELLING THE ARCHIVE. It opened «almost every source below is an INDEX cited by the family tree, not a document this archive has seen» and listed NO ITALIAN CIVIL REGISTER AT ALL; it closed with a section headed «What is not here yet» whose first sentence was «No Italian civil register has been read for this family». Both were true on the day the archive was built and both were months out of date. THE OLD HEADLINE IS KEPT ON THE PAGE, STRUCK, because an archive that quietly deletes its own wrong headline is harder to trust than one that shows the correction. What is actually missing is now narrower and harder: the parish books of Scilla, Piedimonte after 1893, five files at Brisbane, and Zambrone's missing nine years.

source: Open Questions turned into rows, and two answers from yesterday that were never added
scope: Row 119. Two hundred lines of prose -- an inline array for seven questions and five hand-written blocks for others -- which could not be counted or filtered, and which nobody came back to.
result: FIFTEEN QUESTIONS IN data/questions.tsv, RENDERED BY THE KIT'S Questions COMPONENT, whose own comment says the extraction «is research work belonging to each archive rather than something to guess at from outside». FIVE OPEN, TEN ANSWERED. THE BUILDER REFUSES A ROW WITH NO «SETTLES» FIELD -- a question without the record that would answer it is a regret, not a queue item. AND THE EXTRACTION CAUGHT WHAT THE PROSE HID: three questions were headed ANSWERED and still sat undifferentiated beside the open ones; TWO ANSWERED ON 20 SEPTEMBER HAD NEVER BEEN ADDED AT ALL -- Filippo Arena's marriage and how far above him the line goes; and the «Salvatore Mazza in the Sicilian registers» negative, nine indexes across three comuni, has since been OVERTAKEN by Nati 1873 atto 3, so all nine were in the wrong place. The answered questions STAY on the page: one that vanishes when it is settled leaves a reader unable to tell a thing never asked from a thing asked and closed.

source: Antenati — Scilla deaths 1838-1842 read at BOTH A and M for Litteria Morabito
scope: Row 170. She outlived Orazio, who died 12 July 1830, and is named without «fu» in the marriage Tavola of 4 September 1838. Each year read at TWO letters, not one: a married woman can be indexed under her husband's surname or her own.
result: FIVE CONSECUTIVE YEARS, TEN SECTIONS, AND SHE IS IN NONE OF THEM. Every M section is quoted whole on the Scilla reads page -- eight Morabito deaths across the five years, and not one is a Litteria or a Letteria. RECORDED AS PART, NOT DONE, because the window is not closed: Scilla's death series runs to 1865 in the restauration fondo and to 1943 in the Italian one, and she could have died in any of them. Containers are banked to 1844. A BY-PRODUCT WORTH KEEPING: five ARENA deaths turned up in the A sections and NONE belongs to Orazio's household -- Rocco 1838, Giuseppa 1839, Giuseppe and Santo 1841, Giuseppe 1842 -- which is a reminder that the town holds at least seven Arena families and the parents' column is the only thing that separates them.

source: Antenati — the 1714 Piedimonte riveli index read COMPLETE, and the running totals are what made it complete
scope: Row 162. Container qJkjONB, 283 images. Images 1 to 17 are a summary index -- «Nomi | Somme di Lordo | di Netto | Cagione di Riveli | folio» -- alphabetised BY GIVEN NAME, so there is no shortcut to a surname and all of it had to be read.
result: 142 HOUSEHOLDS, AND NO MAZZA AND NO MAZZEO IN ANY OF THEM. THE READING WAS ALMOST A PARTIAL ONE. Twelve index images were read first and two of them, p7 and p9, looked like blank versos at thumbnail size. THE RUNNING TOTALS SAID OTHERWISE: p6 closes at 1468 and p8 opens with a «riporto» of 2556, which is eight households nobody had read; p8 closes at 3774 and p10 opens at 4023. Both pages were fetched at full width and hold entries 73-80 and 106-108. A DOUBLE-ENTRY BOOK CHECKS ITSELF, AND THIS ONE CAUGHT A NEGATIVE THAT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE BEEN ELEVEN HOUSEHOLDS SHORT. SO THE SEQUENCE AT PIEDIMONTE IS: 1714, no Mazzeo and no Mazza; 1747-1748, TWO MAZZEO and no Mazza; the civil registers from 1820, Mazza and no Mazzeo. THAT IS A SHAPE AND NOT A DESCENT, and it is recorded as one: a rivelo is a TAX RETURN and a household can be absent from one without being absent from the town.

source: The estate told about the Antenati name index
scope: Row 140. Not a Mazza finding but an estate one: Falco, Defranceschi and Lerena are reading Italian volumes the same way this archive was before it found the index.
result: SENT TO THE LANDING SITE FOR CIRCULATION, carrying the query form and the three cautions that each cost something here. THE QUERY: /search-nominative/?cognome=X&localita=Y&s_size=100, which returns acts with FATHER, MOTHER AND SPOUSE already extracted. THE CAUTIONS: the ACT TYPE DIFFERS BY COMUNE -- Scilla is indexed for deaths 1911-1943 and PIZZO FOR BIRTHS 1868-1903, so carrying «deaths only» across would produce a confident negative on a series indexed the other way round; «fq=» and «facets=» are SILENTLY IGNORED and return the unfiltered count, which looks like a successful filtered query; and ONLY ROWS WITH A p.morte VALUE ARE THE DECEASED -- the rest are relatives seen from inside somebody else's act, and reading them as deaths invents people with plausible names and dates. Also that «localita=» matches any place attached to a person, not the place of registration.

source: The Crupi given somewhere to live on the site
scope: Row 77. Six documented Crupi -- Angela, her parents Francesco and Maria Vecchio, and her brothers Pietro, Antonino and Mario -- with no page, no section and no place in the four-quarters story, because they arrived through a MARRIAGE rather than a descent. Visible only as rows in a table.
result: A SECTION ON /brisbane/, WHICH IS WHERE THEY ACTUALLY ARE, built from additions.json so it cannot drift from the data. It carries the four things this archive knows about them that the family tree does not: that «ANGELA CUPO» is ANGELA CRUPI, born 20 December 1900; that she had THREE BROTHERS IN QUEENSLAND and nobody knew, all four registrations naming FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO; that PIETRO AND ANTONINO came into Brisbane together on the OTRANTO on 19 August 1930 as consecutive entries in the aliens register, and Angela followed on the VIMINALE in 1937 with two daughters; and that ANTONINO WAS INTERNED AT LOVEDAY, a boot repairer at Ingham with the fourth finger of his right hand deformed, born at PIEDIMONTE ETNEO -- the Mazza's own town. AND THE POINT THE SECTION CLOSES ON: Pietro's missing aliens card looked like a gap and is not one. «Alien Registration Certificate NOT ISSUED», because he was naturalised in 1932. An explained absence and an unexplained one look identical until somebody checks.

source: Antenati name index — ALL 69 Arena deaths at Scilla 1910-1943, pulled and read
scope: Rows 146 and 140. The query was re-run to TEST THE FORM this archive had just broadcast to three other archives -- an untested method note is untested code. It works, and it returns far more than the earlier sweep saw.
result: SIXTY-NINE ARENA, NOT TWENTY-SIX. The earlier sweep worked from twenty-six indexed Arena deaths; the full pull returns 152 rows which deduplicate to about sixty-nine people, every one with parents or spouse. AND THE ANSWER FOR ROW 146 HOLDS AGAINST THE LARGER SET: only TWO carry «Madre Serafina Arlotta» -- ROCCO, 8 February 1932, «Padre Francesco Antonio ... Coniuge Generosa Costa», and GIOVANNI, 31 March 1936, «Padre Antonio ... Coniuge Concetta Russo». FILIPPO AND GIUSEPPE, born 1852 and 1860, ARE IN NONE OF THE SIXTY-NINE. THE «p.morte» CAUTION IS NOW CONFIRMED BY EXAMPLE, not just asserted: the index returns «Rocco Arena -- Figlio Serafina Arena -- Atto di morte 15 Agosto 1912» AND «Serafina Arena -- Morte: Scilla, 15/08/1912 -- Padre Rocco Arena, Madre Generosa Costa». The dead child is Serafina; the first row is her father seen from inside her act. Reading it as his death would have killed Rocco Arena twenty years early, with a plausible date.

source: Antenati name index — NICOTRA at Catania, PROSTAMO at Pizzo, CASSANITI at Catania
scope: Three questions the name index could in principle answer: Maria Nicotra's parents, the Prostamo who stayed at Pizzo, and the real spelling of Venera Cassaneti. EACH ZERO WAS CONTROL-TESTED in the same breath against «Arena at Scilla», which returns 69.
result: ALL THREE ARE REAL NEGATIVES AND NOT THROTTLING. The control returned 69 risultati and 275 links; Prostamo at Pizzo and Cassaniti at Catania each returned «Nessun risultato» with thirty boilerplate links and no result count. A ZERO FROM AN OBJECT NOT VERIFIED IS NOT A NEGATIVE, IT IS NO RESULT -- the Booyzen session's phrasing, adopted. NICOTRA AT CATANIA RETURNS EIGHT DECEASED AND NOT ONE IS HERS: Concetta at Catenanuova, three Giuseppe and a Nunziata at VICOPISANO -- which is in TUSCANY. THAT IS THE «localita=» CAUTION DEMONSTRATED IN THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN DATA: the parameter matches any place attached to a person, not the place of death, so a query scoped to Catania returned people who died four hundred miles away. PROSTAMO AT PIZZO IS THE MORE SURPRISING NIL: Pizzo is name-indexed for BIRTHS 1868-1903 and this family was certainly at Pizzo -- so either the Prostamo had left by 1868 or the indexing does not reach them.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, the 1871 marriage ALLEGATI: four parents certified «vivente»
scope: Row 6 and row 47. The marriage of Rosario Mazza and Leonarda Bonanno (Matrimoni 1871 atto 14) was read on 13 September and the act names all four parents. What had NEVER been opened is the volume beside it -- «Matrimoni, allegati» 1871, container 0noKDq9, 83 images -- so the act was re-read to calibrate the fascicolo numbering and the bundle for act 14 was found at images 43-45.
result: THE TOP OF THE SICILIAN SPINE GETS A DATED PROOF OF LIFE, IN A PRINTED FIELD. Fascicolo 14 holds the «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», published at the door of the Palazzo Comunale on SUNDAY 16 APRIL 1871. The form prints «figlio del ____» and «e della ____» and the clerk filled both blanks with the word VIVENTE: «figlio del VIVENTE MARIANO, professione bracciante, residente anche ivi -- e della VIVENTE MARIA CATALANO, professione industriosa, residente anche ivi», and for the bride «figlia del VIVENTE GAETANO, professione bracciante -- e della VIVENTE ANNA CAVALLARO, professione industriosa». FOUR PEOPLE AT GENERATION SIX, ALL ALIVE, ALL AT PIEDIMONTE, ALL WITH A TRADE -- and for Maria Catalano and Anna Cavallaro it is the FIRST record of a trade at all. MARIANO MAZZA is now documented twice in his own right: declaring Rosario's birth in June 1845 aged thirty-six, and named living and working in April 1871 aged about sixty-two. His death is after 16 April 1871, which is the first bound this archive has ever had on it. AND THE ALLEGATI ARE NOT PROCESSETTI, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the Bourbon-era «Matrimoni, processetti» at Piedimonte carry the spouses' BIRTH EXTRACTS and their dead parents' DEATH ACTS, and this archive has mined them. The Italian-era «Matrimoni, allegati» of 1871 carry the PUBLICATION CERTIFICATE and little else -- no birth extract, no death act. A researcher who reasons from the processetti to the allegati will plan a search that the volume cannot answer. What the allegati DO carry, and the processetti do not, is this printed vivente/fu field. AND THE HONEST COST: the marriage act itself had been read on 13 SEPTEMBER and written out in this very file, and I fetched the whole volume again -- twenty-odd images, the annual index, and a folio-by-folio calibration -- before checking. THE RULE IS THE ONE ROW 145 ALREADY WROTE, POINTING THE OTHER WAY: this archive is now large enough that BEFORE OPENING A VOLUME YOU GREP WHAT HAS BEEN READ. Two hundred and fourteen rows of searched.tsv exist so that the second search never happens, and they only work if somebody reads them.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1847 and 1848, both annual Tavole read end to end
scope: A TEST OF ONE NUMBER. The 1871 marriage act and the publication certificate beside it both make LEONARDA BONANNO «d'anni ventitré compiuti» on 16-30 April 1871, which puts her birth between April 1847 and April 1848. This archive holds her birth act as Piedimonte, Nati 1843 atto 101, 7 November 1843 -- which would make her twenty-seven. Either the age is wrong or there are TWO Leonarda Bonanno and the 1843 girl died. Containers for Nati 1846-1850 were already bought, so the test cost images only. Both annual Tavole read in the original at the child-name column, every entry, no sampling.
result: THE 1843 ACT STANDS AND THE AGE IS FOUR YEARS OUT. 1847 runs 1 to 116 and 1848 runs 1 to 144 -- two hundred and sixty consecutive entries, all read -- and NEITHER YEAR HOLDS A LEONARDA BONANNO. 1847 holds no Bonanno at all; 1848 holds one, BONANNO MARIA at act 99. There is no second Leonarda, so the woman who married Rosario Mazza is the girl born 7 November 1843 and both 1871 documents understate her by four years. AND THE TWO DOCUMENTS ARE NOT TWO WITNESSES. The marriage act and the publication certificate agree on «ventitré», and the agreement is worth nothing: the same uffiziale wrote both, in the same fortnight, from the same declaration. This archive counts independent confirmations, and here is a pair that LOOKS independent -- different volume, different form, different date -- and is one statement written twice. AND THE SWEEP PAID THREE TIMES OVER, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR READING THE WHOLE TAVOLA RATHER THAN SCANNING FOR ONE NAME. (1) Nati 1847 atto 31 is «MAZZA SEBASTIANO -- Mazza Innocenzio / Cavallaro Domenica», the first child ever found for the couple in row 93, whose marriage this archive had written off as possibly unreachable. They were at Piedimonte and having children in 1847. (2) Nati 1848 atto 45 is «CASSANITI VENERA -- Cassaniti Gaetano / Venuti Maria», born the 14th -- the right name, the right town and a plausible date for MARIA NICOTRA'S MOTHER, the woman row 161 has been unable to touch. A candidate, not a conclusion. (3) A NAMESAKE TRAP CAUGHT IN THE ACT. What I first read as «Bonanno Mariano» at 1847 act 30 is «BONACCORSO Mariano», son of BONACCORSO GAETANO and Lucia Grasso -- and 1848 act 46 gives the same couple a Francesco. Piedimonte held a Gaetano Bonanno AND a Gaetano Bonaccorso at the same time, and this archive has ALREADY miscopied one for the other once, in the 1877 and 1880 birth rows of pe-mazza-acts.tsv. The zoom that corrected me is the whole method: I had read the name off a 620-pixel band and it was wrong.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1871: the whole annual index read, and no NICOTRA
scope: Row 161, row 47, row 89. While calibrating the 1871 marriage volume the annual index was read in full -- both openings, both halves of the DUPLICATA, all twenty-six acts accounted for. The question put to it: is the marriage of GIOVANNI NICOTRA and VENERA CASSANITI here?
result: IT IS NOT, AND THE NEGATIVE IS COMPLETE RATHER THAN PARTIAL. The 1871 «Indice Annuale per gli atti DI MATRIMONIO» names BOTH SPOUSES for every act -- groom on the upper line, bride on the lower -- and all twenty-six are legible across two openings: Monte/Cannavò 1, Previtera/Papurri 2, Pagano/Greco 3, Trovato/Spina 4, Difranceso/Cernuto 5, Messina/Parisi 6, Caltabiano/Cardile 7, Maccarone/Intelisano 8, Cavallaro/Cannavò 9, Chiavia/Gambino 10, Maugeri/Zappalardo 11, Cassanoti/Amante 12, Pennisi/Sapienza 13, MAZZA/BONANNO 14, D'Ignoto/Cassumi 15, Cipriano/Pagano 16, Papurri/Mangeri 17, Scandurra/Consolo 18, Cannavò/Caruso 19, Russo/Sanderi 20, Petrino/Ferrito 21, Russo/Fazio 22, Navarro/Costarino 23, Vecchio/Cavallaro 24, Patanè/Guarnera 25, Greco/Cardile 26. NO NICOTRA GROOM AND NO CASSANITI BRIDE. (There IS a «Cassanoti Giovanni» at act 12 -- he marries an AMANTE ROSARIA, not a Cassaniti, and the spelling is a reminder of how loosely this town's clerks handled the name.) AND THIS OPENS A ROUTE ROW 161 HAD NOT GOT. Row 161 spent fourteen consecutive years on the Piedimonte BIRTH indexes hunting Maria Nicotra and found nothing; the MARRIAGE index is a different instrument and a far cheaper one -- ONE PAGE-PAIR PER YEAR, both spouses named, no act need be opened to eliminate a year. Sweeping Piedimonte marriages 1866-1885 for a NICOTRA groom is now a bounded job of about twenty crops. Only the 1871 container is bought; the rest are one batched container lookup away.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20: GIOVANNI NICOTRA and VENERA CASSANITI
scope: Rows 47, 89, 161 and the brand-new row 172. The Piedimonte marriage index names BOTH spouses, one page-pair a year, so a year is eliminated without opening an act. Containers were banked for 1870 and 1872-1875 and the sweep began at 1870. 1870's N section holds one line -- «Nucifora Michele, Lo Coco Nicoletta, 15» -- and 1871's whole index of twenty-six couples had already been read clean. 1872 is the second year tried.
result: FOUND, IN THE SECOND YEAR OF A SWEEP THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN RUN WEEKS AGO. The N section of the 1872 annual index reads «NICOTRA GIOVANNI, E CASSANITI VENERA -- 20», and act 20 is legible whole on one page. «L'anno milleottocento settantadue, nel giorno SETTE del mese di OTTOBRE, alle ore nove antemeridiane, nella Casa Comunale ... sono comparsi GIOVANNI NICOTRA, di anni TRENTUNO, di professione bracciante, DOMICILIATO E RESIDENTE A MASCALI, figlio di ROSARIO, di professione bracciante, e di VENERA MURABITO, contadina, domiciliati e residenti PURE IN MASCALI. E VENERA CASSANITI, di anni VENTIQUATTRO, qui domiciliata e residente, figlia del FU GAETANO, e di FU MARIA CURRENTI.» Witnesses Salvadore Dadone d'Ignoto, 60, and Venerando Papurri FU Ignazio, 41, braccianti. Sindaco Barone Mariano Dottor Vocy. FOUR NEW PEOPLE AT GENERATION SIX, on the two lines this archive called the side nobody has ever searched -- ROSARIO NICOTRA and VENERA MURABITO of Mascali, both living; GAETANO CASSANITI and MARIA CURRENTI of Piedimonte, both dead. The «fu» is doing real work here and it is CONTROL-TESTED INSIDE THE ACT ITSELF: the same clerk writes «Venerando Papurri FU Ignazio» two lines above, so its absence over the Nicotra parents is a statement and not an omission. AND IT EXPLAINS FOURTEEN EMPTY YEARS. Row 161 read the Piedimonte birth indexes of 1870 through 1883 -- fourteen consecutive annual indexes, every N section quoted -- hunting Maria Nicotra, and the Nicotra are there the whole time and never produce her. THE REASON IS IN THIS ACT: her father was a MASCALI man. A wife went to her husband's comune, so the children of this marriage were registered at MASCALI, a comune this archive has never opened and never listed. The Catania hypothesis was not needed and the tree's «born Piedimonte» is her mother's town, not hers. AND THE IDENTIFICATION IS NOT CIRCULAR, WHICH MATTERS BECAUSE «Giovanni Nicotra» IS A COMMON NAME. The family's own export -- parsed long before any of this -- gives John Nicotra and Venera Cassaneti SEVEN children, and one of them is a ROSARIO NICOTRA. A first son takes the paternal grandfather's name, and the paternal grandfather in this act is Rosario. The archive held the grandson's name for years and could not have derived the grandfather's from it. Add the bride's uncommon surname, her age fitting Nati 1848 atto 45 to the year, and the province, and the join carries. ONE LOOSE END, LEFT OPEN: the 1898 marriage proclamation at Piedimonte calls Maria Nicotra's mother «MONTI VENERA».
