That is now a three-way conflict -- Monti, Cassaneti, Cassaniti -- and this act settles only the second and third. Row 89 keeps it.

source: Antenati — MASCALI listed whole, and MARIA NICOTRA'S BIRTH ACT found in the second year read
scope: Row 173, opened an hour earlier off the 1872 marriage act, which put Giovanni Nicotra «domiciliato e residente a MASCALI». Mascali had never been listed, never been searched and was not in any ark bank. Listed with ?localita=Mascali&s_size=500, then the annual birth indexes read at the N section -- 1873 first (the year after the marriage), then 1875 (the year the Queensland death registration implies).
result: THE LISTING IS COMPLETE AND SAYS SO. 498 results, 498 distinct arks, and the facets read «Archivio di Stato di Catania (452)» and «Archivio di Stato di Palermo (46)» -- 452+46=498, so this is the whole holding and not a sample at the ceiling. All 498 rows are written to data/mascali-arks.tsv rather than summarised, because the listing costs a rate-limited page load and the second one is the expensive one. WHAT MASCALI HAS. Civil registration 1820-1893, the same span as Piedimonte: restaurazione 1820-1865 (Nati, Morti, Matrimoni, Nati esposti, Diversi, and from 1841 the MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI with their birth extracts), italiano 1866-1893. AND FORTY-SIX VOLUMES AT PALERMO that are not civil registration at all: RIVELI DI BENI E DI ANIME from the Tribunale del Real Patrimonio for 1616, 1625, 1636, 1652 and 1676-78, and RIVELI DI ANIME E DI TERRE from the Deputazione del Regno for 1714 and 1747-1752 in twenty-nine volumes. Piedimonte's riveli begin in 1714; MASCALI'S BEGIN IN 1616, a century earlier, and this archive has an instrument for reading them. ONE GAP RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: the restaurazione run has NO 1844 -- it goes 1843, then 1845, in every series. 1873 CONFIRMED THE TOWN ON THE FIRST TRY. Its index is alphabetical AND carries a PATERNITA column, so a household identifies itself without opening an act. The N section: Nicotra Giovanni 23 February (padre Giuseppe), Neri Giuseppe 20 March (Salvatore), Nicotra Grazia 29 June (Alfio), Nicolosi Angelo 14 October (Giuseppe), and NICOTRA VENERA, 12 DECEMBER 1873, PATERNITA GIOVANNI -- fourteen months after the marriage, and the family's own export gives Giovanni and Venera a daughter VENERA. THEN 1875, AND IT IS HER. The 1875 index has no paternita column, so the act had to be opened. «Nicotra Maria -- 144». Nati 1875 atto 144, read in the original: «L'anno milleottocento settantacinque, addi DIECI di DICEMBRE, a ore antemeridiane otto e minuti quindici, nella Casa comunale. Avanti di me Gaetano Sacla, Sindaco ed Ufficiale dello Stato Civile del Comune di MASCALI, e comparso GIOVANNI NICOTRA, di anni ventotto, lavorante, domiciliato in Mascali, il quale mi ha dichiarato che alle ore pomeridiane NOVE e minuti TRENTA, del di OTTO del corrente mese, nella casa posta in contrada Sopra Pietrafitta al numero ..., da VENERA CASSANITI sua moglie, ambedue residenti in questo Comune di Mascali, e nata una bambina di sesso femminile che egli mi presenta, e a cui da il nome di MARIA.» Witnesses Gaetano Cardillo, 30, and Salvatore Leo, 30, both lavoranti. MARIA NICOTRA WAS BORN AT MASCALI ON 8 DECEMBER 1875 AT HALF PAST NINE IN THE EVENING. She died at Brisbane in 1963 aged eighty-eight, which the date fits exactly. The tree's «born Piedimonte Etneo» is her mother's town. ONE DISCREPANCY, RECORDED NOT HIDDEN: her father is «di anni trentuno» at his marriage in October 1872 and «di anni ventotto» here in December 1875 -- six years the wrong way in three years. Declared ages, again, and of the same kind as Leonarda Bonanno's four. THE IDENTIFICATION DOES NOT REST ON HIS AGE: it rests on the wife, VENERA CASSANITI, an uncommon pairing named in both acts, on the comune, and on a birth date that matches her Queensland death to the year.

source: Antenati — Mascali births 1874, 1876 and 1877 swept for the other Nicotra children
scope: Row 173. Giovanni Nicotra and Venera Cassaniti married 7 October 1872 and the family's own export gives them SEVEN children -- Maria, Rosa, Venera, Nina, Angela, Rosario, Antonina. Two are now placed: Venera (Nati 1873) and Maria (Nati 1875 atto 144). The years either side were read at the N section, every entry.
result: ONE TRUE NEGATIVE AND TWO YEARS THAT CANNOT BE CALLED EITHER WAY -- AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A COLUMN. 1874's index HAS a «PATERNITA» column, so the year answers the question directly. Its N section is two lines: «Neri Francesco, 1 marzo 1874, Domenico» and «NICOTRA MARIA, 28 detto, GAETANO». NO CHILD OF GIOVANNI IN 1874 -- a real negative, because the instrument names the father. AND THAT SAME LINE IS THE NAMESAKE TRAP CAUGHT IN THE ACT: Mascali registered TWO MARIA NICOTRAS EIGHTEEN MONTHS APART, one to a Gaetano in March 1874 and ours to Giovanni in December 1875. An index entry alone would have been a coin toss; opening act 144 is the only reason the right one is on the spine. 1876 AND 1877 HAVE NO PATERNITA COLUMN, and that changes the status of the reading completely. 1876's N section is five lines -- Neri Giuseppe 25, NICOTRA GIUSEPPA 81, Nicolosi Mariano 87, Nicolosi Rosario 144, Neri Lucia 170. 1877's is three -- NICOTRA MARIANO 10, NICOTRA ROSARIA 8, Nucifora Mariano 132. «Giuseppa» is not among the seven children the export names, so 1876 is probably not theirs; «ROSARIA» in 1877 may well be the ROSA the export carries. BUT NEITHER YEAR CAN BE SETTLED WITHOUT OPENING THE ACTS, and until they are opened these are READ AND UNRESOLVED -- not negatives. That is the status row 171 says this archive cannot currently write, and here are three years that need it. 1877's N section also ENDS AT THE FOOT OF ITS COLUMN, which is where this archive has produced a false negative before: the next column was checked and begins at P, so the section is complete at three entries. Acts 8 and 10 of 1877 fall within days of each other in January, so they are either twins or two households -- another reason not to guess.

source: Antenati name index — this archive's own nils re-tested with the suspect parameter removed
scope: Acting on the Lerena archive's caution that a control licenses the SHAPE of a query and says nothing about the VALUE -- its own parent-pair zero survived a passing control and was false, because the mother's surname sat unparsed in a given-name field. This archive has four name-index nils on record. Each was re-run with «localita» REMOVED, and the raw page inspected rather than a count regex.
result: THE NILS STAND, THE METHOD THAT TESTED THEM DID NOT, AND THE MEANING OF THE NILS WAS WRONG. (1) THEY ARE GENUINE. «cognome=Cassaniti» with no locality at all returns «NESSUN RISULTATO TROVATO. La tua ricerca per nome non ha prodotto risultati!» -- prose, not a count. Same for Prostamo. Musolino at Scilla still returns 7, so the form works. The extra parameter was NOT hiding anything here. (2) BUT THE DETECTOR WAS BROKEN AND GOT THE RIGHT ANSWER BY ACCIDENT. This archive reads a result count by matching «N risultati». THE ZERO PAGE DOES NOT CONTAIN THAT STRING AT ALL -- it is a 266 KB page whose count is a sentence. So «no match» from the regex was indistinguishable from a throttled page, a broken selector or a real zero, and the three were told apart only because the link count was also taken. ANY ZERO FROM THIS INSTRUMENT MUST BE CONFIRMED BY THE PRESENCE OF «Nessun risultato trovato», NOT BY THE ABSENCE OF A COUNT. (3) AND THE INTERPRETATION WAS THE REAL ERROR. «Cassaniti returns nothing» was recorded on 21 September as a real negative about this family. IT IS NOT A FACT ABOUT THE FAMILY. Within hours of that entry this archive read CASSANITI GAETANO in the Piedimonte birth Tavola of 1848 and VENERA CASSANITI in two acts -- Piedimonte Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 and Mascali Nati 1875 atto 144. The people are demonstrably in the registers and the name index returns zero for them ACROSS THE WHOLE OF ITALY. The explanation is already in this archive's own coverage notes: Piedimonte and Mascali are NOT NAME-INDEXED. So the nil means «this comune has not been indexed», not «this person is not there», and the two look identical from inside the query. THAT IS THE STATUS ROW 171 IS ABOUT, demonstrated against this archive's own data three hours after the nil was filed: an instrument was read correctly, the source was empty, and the emptiness was a fact about the INSTRUMENT.

source: A checker for the nils — 27 of this archive's own cannot be checked by a reader
scope: The Lerena archive put its own coverage failures beside this archive's and found that «not covered» is THREE different faults rendering ONE identical empty page: at the COLLECTION (the corpus holds no parish registers at all), at the QUERY SHAPE (a compound surname exact matching cannot reach), and at a SINGLE FIELD (a value the source failed to parse, which then excludes the records that display it). Only the third is ever evidence about a family. And the part of a nil that ages well is neither the query nor the count -- it is the sentence saying WHAT THE INSTRUMENT COULD HAVE REACHED. Only one of that archive's four published nulls survived scrutiny, and it survived because its control had established the parish books were indexed and dated.
result: WRITTEN AS tools/check_nils.py AND RUN AGAINST THIS ARCHIVE, WHICH IT DOES NOT FLATTER. Of 220 searched rows, 173 assert no nil, 20 assert a nil AND say what the instrument could reach -- AND 27 ASSERT A NIL WITH NO REACHABILITY SENTENCE AT ALL. They may every one be sound. The point is that a reader cannot tell, and neither can this archive a week later: «Trove -- Prostamo before 1954», «Find a Grave -- Prostamo and Melluso across Australia», «TNA Discovery -- every surname and town of this family», «Antenati -- Archivio di Stato di Messina, whole province». Each of those is a sentence about a family that may be a sentence about a search engine. THE CHECKER CANNOT JUDGE WHETHER THE SENTENCE IS TRUE -- only somebody who checked the coverage knows that -- so it is ADVISORY and exits 0. It makes the gap visible and finite instead of invisible and assumed empty, which is the same job check_grades.py does for dashed parent edges. It is wired into the build after check:searched. AND THE HONEST NOTE ABOUT ITS OWN ACCURACY: the nil-detecting regex is deliberately narrow and the reachability regex deliberately broad, so it will UNDER-report rather than over-report. A row it passes is not certified; a row it flags is worth a minute. AND THE NUMBER 27 WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE TOOL TURNED ON ITS AUTHOR. It was published straight out of a regex written the same hour and never tested against the rows it judges. Testing it took twenty minutes and moved it to NINE. THREE KINDS OF ERROR, ALL MINE. (1) THE NIL PATTERN MATCHED ROWS FULL OF FINDINGS: «not one» caught «NOT ONE AT NUDGEE» inside a Find a Grave row that reports ELEVEN BURIALS with plot numbers. A checker built to catch unfalsifiable claims had made one. (2) THE REACH PATTERN MISSED PLAIN ENGLISH: three rows state their boundary perfectly -- «BT 26 and BT 27 cover UK PORTS ONLY», «CIVIL REGISTRATION IN THE PROVINCE OF MESSINA BEGINS IN 1820», «this family moved Italy to Australia and never through Britain» -- and were flagged because the word «coverage» was absent. The fix was to look for a BOUNDARY of place, date or record type rather than for a vocabulary. (3) AND I THEN WROTE THAT IT WOULD «UNDER-REPORT RATHER THAN OVER-REPORT», WHICH WAS BACKWARDS. It over-reported by three to one. THREE ROWS HAVE SINCE BEEN GIVEN THE SENTENCE THEY LACKED, and two of them needed it badly: the Piedimonte birth-index sweeps for Maria Nicotra now say outright that the instrument could only ever reach children registered at Piedimonte, and she was registered at MASCALI. NINE REMAIN.

source: Antenati — Mascali, Nati 1841 and 1847: Giovanni Nicotra is in neither
scope: Row 173. Giovanni Nicotra gave TWO ages three years apart -- «di anni trentuno» at his marriage on 7 October 1872 (born about 1841) and «di anni ventotto» at his daughter Maria's birth on 10 December 1875 (born about 1847). His own birth act would settle which, and would carry his parents ROSARIO NICOTRA and VENERA MURABITO independently of the marriage act. Both candidate years were read at Mascali. THE INSTRUMENT: the Bourbon-era «Tavola Alfabetica annuale de' Nati», alphabetical by surname, with columns Num d'ordine, Cognomi e Nomi de' NATI, PATRIA, Cognomi e Nomi de' GENITORI, Giorno della Nascita. IT NAMES BOTH PARENTS, so a Giovanni Nicotra of Rosario and Venera Murabito would identify itself without an act being opened.
result: HE IS IN NEITHER, AND BOTH SECTIONS ARE COMPLETE. 1841's N section is ONE LINE: «87. Nicolosi Salvadore -- Nicolosi Francesco / Mercurio Francesca -- 24 Dicembre 1841». The O section beneath it is empty and the page ends. 1847's N section is TWO LINES: «3. Nicolosi Domenico -- Nicolosi D. Francesco / Mercurio D.a Francesca -- 3 Gennaio 1847» and «69. NICOTRA MARIA -- Nicotra Alfio / Sudani Carmela -- 23 Luglio 1847». Then an empty O section, then P. In both years the section's END was checked in the next letter before anything was written down, which is the rule this archive has already paid for twice. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It establishes that NO GIOVANNI NICOTRA WAS REGISTERED AT MASCALI IN 1841 OR 1847 -- the only two years his own two statements point to. It does NOT establish that he was born elsewhere: this archive has now watched the same man lose six years between two acts, and Leonarda Bonanno lose four between a birth act and a marriage, so a declared age is a bracket and not a date. THE NEXT STEP IS THE REST OF THE BRACKET: Mascali Nati 1838-1850, ten more annual Tavole, each one crop. THE REACH, STATED: these are Mascali's own birth registers for those two years, read at the only section that could hold him, in a table that names both parents. If he was born in another comune -- and his wife's household was at Piedimonte, eight kilometres away -- no Mascali Tavola will ever hold him. AND ONE NAME WORTH REMEMBERING: NICOTRA ALFIO fathered a Maria at Mascali in 1847, and an ALFIO NICOTRA fathered the 1875 Piedimonte Maria Nicotra who is NOT ours. Not pursued, not claimed.

source: The Atlas layers checked — a ramp in the wrong order, a colour decided by row order, and Zambrone missing
scope: A peer session added three Atlas layers to this repository (commit 80ce21e, tools/atlas.py and site/src/pages/atlas.astro, nothing else touched) and explicitly left one judgement to this archive. The commit was pulled and read rather than accepted: the diff, the ramp, the join key, and every count it asserts.
result: THE WORK IS SOUND AND THREE THINGS WERE WRONG. (1) THE RAMP WAS IN THE WRONG ORDER, which was the judgement offered. It had `route` as WORSE than `partial`. build_coverage.py's own docstring defines `route` as «reachable, but through a different archive» and `partial` as «the listing itself is incomplete, so NOTHING IS SETTLED», and the rows bear it out: `route` is Piedimonte past 1893, waiting in the Tribunale's duplicate for Catania, named and findable; `partial` is Briatico, EIGHTY-ONE ROWS HELD AGAINST FIVE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-FIVE AVAILABLE, where nobody knows what is in the rest. A known errand beats not knowing what you are looking at. Swapped, and both labels rewritten to say which is which. (2) A BUG NEITHER OF US HAD LOOKED FOR, AND IT IS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN FAVOURITE SHAPE. A comune has one coverage row PER SERIES and they disagree -- Piedimonte has SIX `open` and one `route`. The code assigned with `=`, so the colour was decided by WHICHEVER ROW SAT LAST IN THE FILE. It rendered correctly for all seven comuni on the day it was written, and would have turned Piedimonte green the moment somebody appended an `open` row beneath its `route` one. A silent change of meaning caused by the ORDER OF A DATA FILE. Fixed to take the WORST status, ranked explicitly, and TESTED BY REVERSING coverage.json AND RE-RUNNING: byte-identical output, seven comuni unchanged. (3) ZAMBRONE IS NOT ON THE MAP AT ALL, which is why twelve of thirteen coverage rows matched and not thirteen. The reason is structural and bigger than the Atlas: THE MAP'S PLACES COME FROM THE EXPORT'S PEOPLE, and Zambrone holds no exported person. Its people -- the whole Ventrice line -- exist only in documented-additions.tsv, which now runs to 115 rows and includes every person this archive has added from a register: Mariano Mazza, Maria Catalano, Rosario Nicotra, Venera Murabito, Gaetano Cassaniti, Maria Currenti. ALL OF THEM ARE INVISIBLE ON THE ATLAS. The counts the peer asserted were checked and are right: 18 of 20 burials land on a drawn place, the two that do not are Arneytown, and the coverage join is on the same `head()` the roster uses, which work-list 158 says is the thing that silently drops people when it changes.

source: The reversal test run across this archive's own builders — one real fault, in the questions
scope: The Atlas fold bug found yesterday was a many-to-one join written with `=`, invisible because it rendered correctly on the day it was written. The peer session that introduced it checked its own estate for more of the class and found none. THIS ARCHIVE OWED ITSELF THE SAME CHECK, and by hand rather than by eye: tools/check_order.py reverses each data/*.tsv, re-runs the builder that reads it, and compares the output.
result: EIGHT BUILDER/INPUT PAIRS TESTED, ONE REAL FAULT, AND IT WAS IN THE QUESTIONS. build_questions.py numbered each question with `enumerate(rows, start=1)` -- THE ROW'S POSITION -- and the kit RENDERS that number, as «{r.n ?? i + 1}». So inserting a question anywhere but the end silently renumbered every question below it, and anyone who cited «question 7» was pointing at a different question the next day. Nothing had gone wrong yet and nothing would have looked wrong when it did. FIXED THE WAY THE WORK LIST ALREADY DOES IT: `n` is now an explicit column in questions.tsv, assigned once and never reused, and the builder REFUSES a row whose `n` is missing, non-numeric or duplicated -- both refusals tested by breaking the file on purpose. All eight pairs now give identical output on reversed input. AND THE TEST ITSELF HAD TO BE FIXED TWICE BEFORE IT WAS WORTH TRUSTING. (1) It read the source file INSIDE `open(src, "w")`, which truncates first, so it got an empty file and died; the restore in `finally` is the only reason that cost nothing. (2) FAR MORE IMPORTANT, IT FIRST COMPARED BYTES, and six of eight pairs «failed» because most of these builders emit a LIST in file order -- reversing the input reverses the list, the bytes differ, and every one of those six was benign. A BYTE COMPARISON CANNOT TELL PRESENTATION FROM DATA LOSS. The fault worth catching is a fold in which one row overwrites another, and that shows up as a CHANGED VALUE or a VANISHED KEY, never as a reordering. The test now canonicalises both outputs by sorting every list by its own contents and compares the SET OF FACTS. Six false alarms became one true one. NOT WIRED INTO `npm run build`, deliberately: it temporarily rewrites tracked data files and restores them in a `finally`, which survives an exception but not a kill, and a build killed mid-check would leave a reversed data file looking like an edit. It is `npm run check:order`, run on purpose. AND A QUESTION WENT GREEN ON THE WAY PAST: «Where was Maria Nicotra born?» had been open since the archive was built and was answered this morning -- MASCALI, Nati 1875 atto 144. Four open now, not five.

source: Antenati — Mascali, the hunt for Rosario Nicotra's household: Matrimoni 1840 clean, and a torn Tavola
scope: Row 173, reaching for GENERATION SEVEN. Rosario Nicotra and Venera Murabito are known only from inside their son's marriage act of 1872. Their OWN marriage would name all four of THEIR parents, because Mascali's restauration marriage Tavola is alphabetical by groom and carries a four-line parents column -- groom's father, groom's mother, bride's father, bride's mother -- with the dead marked «fu». One Tavola read per year. Giovanni was born about 1841 or 1847 on his own two statements, so the marriage brackets to roughly 1830-1845.
result: 1840 IS A CLEAN NEGATIVE AND THE METHOD IS PROVED. The Tavola of Matrimoni 1840 is alphabetical, names both spouses and ALL FOUR PARENTS, and its N section is ONE ENTRY: «10. Nicolosi Francesco / Mercurio Francesca -- Nicolosi Domenico, Mercurio Angela, Mercurio Pietro, Bassi Maria». The section's end was checked on the facing page, which opens at P. NO NICOTRA MARRIAGE AT MASCALI IN 1840. AND A CHANGE OF PLAN WORTH RECORDING. Hunting one marriage across fifteen years is the expensive way; the BIRTH Tavole name both parents too, so a single «Nicotra [X] -- Nicotra Rosario / Murabito Venera» would place the household AND bracket the marriage from below. That is the sweep to run, and its containers are banked: Mascali Nati 1839, 1840, 1841, 1842, 1843, 1845, 1846, 1847, 1848, plus Matrimoni 1840 -- FIFTEEN MASCALI CONTAINERS NOW HELD, so the remaining work is reading rather than rate-limited fetching. AND ONE PHYSICAL CONDITION THAT IS NOT A NEGATIVE. THE 1842 BIRTH TAVOLA IS TORN, and the archive's own card says so: «Torn Page(s)». The surviving leaf carries the R and S sections with the head of the page lost, and the M-to-P run sits on the damaged side. 1842 CANNOT BE READ AS A NEGATIVE FOR NICOTRA -- the section that would hold them is missing, not empty. Recorded as a condition of the volume rather than a result, which is the distinction row 171 exists for. THE REACH, STATED: 1840's marriage Tavola is Mascali's own, complete, alphabetical, and names four parents a couple; it can only ever answer for marriages celebrated AT MASCALI in that year. If Rosario Nicotra married in his wife's comune, no Mascali Tavola will hold it.

source: Antenati — Mascali births 1839–1848, every N section read: the only Nicotra at Mascali is ALFIO'S
scope: Row 173. Giovanni Nicotra is «domiciliato e residente a MASCALI» at his marriage in 1872 and his parents ROSARIO NICOTRA and VENERA MURABITO are «residenti pure in Mascali», yet he is in neither of the two years his own declared ages point to. The question this sweep puts: WAS ROSARIO'S HOUSEHOLD AT MASCALI AT ALL in the 1840s? The instrument answers it directly, because Mascali's Bourbon-era «Tavola Alfabetica annuale de' Nati» is alphabetical by surname and NAMES BOTH PARENTS -- so a single «Nicotra [X] -- Nicotra Rosario / Murabito Venera» would settle it without an act being opened. Every surviving year of the decade was read at the N section, and in each the section's END was checked into the next letter before anything was written down.
result: NINE YEARS, EIGHT READABLE, AND ROSARIO NICOTRA'S HOUSEHOLD IS IN NONE OF THEM. 1839: THERE IS NO N SECTION AT ALL -- M (Musumeci, Marano, Maccarrone, Mangano, Mercurio, Marchese, Mannino) runs straight into P (Patane), so not one child of any N surname was born at Mascali that year. 1840: three entries -- NICOTRA VENERA (padre ALFIO, madre Carmela Sudieri, 11 May), Nicolosi Mariancola (Nicolosi Francesco / Mercurio Gioacchina), Nicolosi Leonardo (Nicolosi Salvadore / Finocchiaro Venera). 1841: one entry, Nicolosi Salvadore (Nicolosi Francesco / Mercurio Francesca, 24 December). 1842: THE VOLUME IS TORN and the archive's own card says so; the surviving leaf carries R and S with the head of the page lost and the M-to-P run on the damaged side. NOT READABLE, AND NOT A NEGATIVE. 1843: the N section is HEADED AND COMPLETELY EMPTY, and so is the O beneath it. 1845: one entry, Nicolosi Giovanna (Nicolosi Salvadore / Finocchiaro Venera, 22 April). 1846: N HEADED AND EMPTY again. 1847: two entries, Nicolosi Domenico and NICOTRA MARIA (padre ALFIO, madre Sudani Carmela, 23 July). 1848: one entry, Neri Antonina (Neri Leonardo / Borzi Maria, 11 July). (1844 does not exist in this series at all -- the gap recorded when Mascali was listed.) SO THE ONLY NICOTRA HOUSEHOLD AT MASCALI IN THAT DECADE IS ALFIO NICOTRA AND CARMELA SUDIERI, who appear in 1840 and again in 1847. ROSARIO NICOTRA AND VENERA MURABITO ARE ABSENT FROM EVERY READABLE YEAR. WHAT THAT MEANS, STATED CAREFULLY. It does NOT mean they are not the people named in the 1872 act -- that act is read and unambiguous. It means THEY WERE NOT AT MASCALI IN THE 1840s, and therefore GIOVANNI NICOTRA WAS ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT BORN THERE. The household came to Mascali between about 1848 and 1872. His birthplace is a comune this archive has not yet identified, and the way to it is his own marriage ALLEGATI -- the 1872 publication certificate, which in this province prints the spouses' birthplaces -- not another Mascali sweep. THE REACH, STATED: these are Mascali's own birth registers for nine consecutive years, read at the only section that could hold the surname, in a table that names both parents. They can answer for Mascali and for nothing else. AND ALFIO NICOTRA IS WORTH A LINE: an ALFIO NICOTRA also fathered the 1875 Piedimonte Maria Nicotra who is NOT ours. Whether the Mascali Alfio and the Piedimonte Alfio are one man is untested and nothing is claimed.

source: Antenati — the 1872 marriage allegati: GIOVANNI NICOTRA WAS BORN AT GIARRE
scope: Nine consecutive Mascali birth Tavole, 1839-1848, put Rosario Nicotra's household nowhere in the town, so Giovanni was not born there and the question became WHERE. The instrument was already proved this morning on Rosario Mazza: the Italian-era «Matrimoni, allegati» hold a printed «CERTIFICATO DI SEGUITA PUBBLICAZIONE DI MATRIMONIO» which, in the 1872 form, prints «nato a ____» SEPARATELY FROM «residente a ____» for each spouse. Piedimonte's 1872 allegati, container LDmQaWG, 85 images.
result: «NATO A GIARRE», AND A SIXTH TOWN ENTERS THE ARCHIVE. The bundle for act 20 is at images 71-74, found by reading a neighbouring certificate rather than by hunting wrapper numbers -- image 65 is fascicolo 19, «Salvadore Scipelliti (nato a BRONTE) e Antonia Zumbo (nata a Piedimonte Etneo)», which matches the annual index entry for act 19 and fixes the count. THE CERTIFICATE, read in the original: «TRA GIOVANNI NICOTRA -- NATO A GIARRE -- residente a MASCALI -- di professione bracciante -- di eta anni TRENTUNO -- figlio di ROSARIO, di professione bracciante, residente a Mascali, e di VENERA MURABITO, di professione contadina, residente a Mascali. E VENERA CASSANITI -- NATA A PIEDIMONTE ETNEO -- residente a Piedimonte Etneo -- di professione contadina -- di eta anni VENTIQUATTRO -- figlia di FU GAETANO e di FU MARIA CURRENTI.» Published at Mascali, «Fatto oggi in Mascali il di CINQUE del mese di SETTEMBRE dell'anno 1872», signed Di Leonardo -- the groom's own comune, as the code required. THE WHOLE SHAPE OF THE SICILIAN QUARTER IS NOW VISIBLE: Giovanni Nicotra born at GIARRE about 1841, living at MASCALI by 1872 with his parents; Venera Cassaniti born at PIEDIMONTE ETNEO in 1848; married at Piedimonte 7 October 1872; their daughter MARIA born at MASCALI 8 December 1875; Maria marries Salvatore Mazza of Piedimonte about 1900 and dies at Brisbane in 1963. FOUR COMUNI IN ONE WOMAN'S DESCENT, and the family tree recorded one of them. AND IT EXPLAINS THE NINE EMPTY MASCALI YEARS EXACTLY: the household came from Giarre, which is the next comune down the coast.

source: Antenati — GIARRE listed whole, and s_size=500 is a PAGE, not a ceiling
scope: Giarre had never been listed. The first query, ?localita=Giarre&s_size=500, returned 500 arks and a facet total of 808 -- the exact trap this archive's own note warns about, a listing sitting at the ceiling and therefore a SAMPLE rather than a holding.
result: AND THE CEILING TURNS OUT NOT TO BE ONE. «&s_page=2» returns the remaining 308, and 500+308 = 808 = the facet total exactly. THIS ARCHIVE'S STANDING NOTE WAS WRONG: s_size=500 is a PAGE SIZE, not a limit on what can be retrieved, and any holding larger than 500 is reachable in two loads instead of being permanently a sample. THE CORRECTION MATTERS BEYOND GIARRE: Briatico is recorded in antenati-coverage.tsv as «THE WORST UNDER-LISTING IN THE ARCHIVE: eighty-one rows held against 555 available», and that under-listing was accepted as a wall. IT IS NOT A WALL. It is two page loads. GIARRE'S HOLDING, banked whole in data/giarre-arks.tsv: 808 volumes, ALL AT CATANIA, 1820-1873, and it is a bigger comune than any other in this archive -- 164 Nati volumes, 147 Morti, 131 Matrimoni, 44 Matrimoni processetti, 42 Matrimoni allegati, plus Cittadinanze and their allegati. IT HOLDS TWO COPIES OF EVERY YEAR -- e.g. Nati 1841 as an_ua68999 (segnatura 15941) and an_ua19993253 (segnatura 16345) -- so a damaged or missing leaf in one may survive in the other, which is a resource this archive has not had anywhere else. AND UNLIKE MASCALI IT HAS 1844. FIRST YEAR READ: Nati 1841, container 5dZj97v, 226 images, annual Tavola alphabetical at the back. ITS M SECTION RUNS STRAIGHT INTO O -- THERE IS NO N SECTION AT ALL -- so no Nicotra was born at Giarre in 1841. (A row I first read as «Nicolosi Salvadore» at 207 is MIGLIERINO Salvadore, still in M; corrected at full width before anything was written down.) His two declared ages differ by six years, so the window 1838-1848 must be swept, not the single year.

source: Antenati — GIARRE births 1838–1848, every N section read: the only Nicotra there is a DON
scope: Row 177. The 1872 publication certificate says Giovanni Nicotra was «NATO A GIARRE», and his two declared ages differ by six years, so the window is a bracket and not a year. Eleven consecutive annual Tavole read at the N section — 1838 to 1848, every year the series holds. Giarre's Tavola is alphabetical and NAMES BOTH PARENTS, so a Nicotra of a ROSARIO would identify itself without an act being opened.
result: ROSARIO NICOTRA'S HOUSEHOLD IS IN NONE OF THE ELEVEN YEARS. The N section is ABSENT ALTOGETHER in 1838, 1840, 1841, 1842 and 1845 — the alphabet runs M straight into O or P. It is WRITTEN AND LEFT EMPTY in 1839, 1843 and 1844, which proves the clerks did write the heading when they had anything to put under it. Three years hold one entry each: 1846 «NICOTRA SALVADORE — Giarre — Nicotra D.r D. ALFIO / CONSOLI D.na ANTONINA — 5 Novembre»; 1847 «NICOLOSI Giuseppe — Nicolosi Angelo / Leotta Gaetana — 31 Gennaio»; and 1848 «110. NICOTRA SALVATORE — ivi — Nicotra D.r D. ALFIO / CONSOLI D.na ANTONINA — 2 Gennaro». THE ONLY NICOTRA HOUSEHOLD AT GIARRE IN ELEVEN YEARS IS A TITLED ONE — «Dottor Don» Alfio Nicotra and «Donna» Antonina Consoli — and they name a Salvatore twice, fourteen months apart, which is what a family does when the first child dies. ROSARIO NICOTRA IS A BRACCIANTE in his son's marriage act. Different household, different class. AND A STRUCTURAL FAULT FOUND IN THE PAPER, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW IS «part» AND NOT «done». The Osservazioni column of the 1848 N entry reads, in the clerk's own hand, «IN FINE DELL'ALFABETO RIPORTATA ALTRA VOLTA LA LETTERA M» — at the end of the alphabet the letter M is entered a second time. GIARRE'S TAVOLE APPEND EXTRA LETTER-SECTIONS AFTER Z, for acts registered late. 1848 appends F and M; 1841 appends F and B; 1842 and 1843 append others still. SO «THE ALPHABET REACHED Z» IS NOT THE END OF THE INDEX, and a negative taken from the main run alone is incomplete. FIVE TAILS HAVE BEEN CHECKED AND ARE CLEAN of any second N — 1838, 1839, 1840, 1841 and 1848. SIX HAVE NOT: 1842, 1843, 1844, 1845, 1846 and 1847. Until those six tails are read this is eleven years swept and five years finished, and it is recorded that way. THE REACH, STATED: these are Giarre's own birth registers for eleven consecutive years, read at the only section that could hold the surname, in a table that names both parents. They answer for Giarre and for nothing else. AND ONE NAME KEEPS RECURRING: ALFIO. The only Nicotra household at MASCALI in 1839-1848 is Alfio Nicotra's; the only one at GIARRE is Dr Don Alfio Nicotra's; and an ALFIO NICOTRA fathered the 1875 Piedimonte Maria Nicotra who is NOT ours. Three Alfio Nicotras within eight kilometres. Nothing is claimed from it.

source: Antenati — the six remaining Giarre tails read: the 1838–1848 sweep is COMPLETE
scope: The Giarre sweep was filed «part» because the 1848 index says in its own Osservazioni column «IN FINE DELL'ALFABETO RIPORTATA ALTRA VOLTA LA LETTERA M» -- these Tavole APPEND EXTRA LETTER-SECTIONS AFTER Z for acts registered late, so reaching Z is not reaching the end of the index. Five tails had been checked; six had not. All six are now read: 1842, 1843, 1844, 1845, 1846 and 1847.
result: NOT ONE OF THE SIX CARRIES AN APPENDED N, AND THE SWEEP IS FINISHED. The appendices are real and they are various: 1842 appends T, P, B and F across images 223-224; 1843 appends R, M, C, G and T across 240-242; 1844 appends a single G on its last image; 1845 appends F and T; AND TWO YEARS APPEND NOTHING AT ALL -- 1846 ends at Z (Zappala Benedetta, Alfio, Giuseppe) with a blank facing page, and 1847 ends at Z with two further Zappala on the last leaf. SO THE APPENDIX IS A HABIT AND NOT A RULE, which is itself worth knowing: its absence in a volume is not evidence that the reading is complete, because 1846 and 1847 look identical to a volume whose appendix simply has not been reached. ALL ELEVEN YEARS ARE NOW VERIFIED IN BOTH THE MAIN RUN AND THE TAIL: 1838, 1839, 1840, 1841, 1842, 1843, 1844, 1845, 1846, 1847, 1848. ROSARIO NICOTRA'S HOUSEHOLD IS IN NONE OF THEM, and the only Nicotra at Giarre in eleven years remains «Nicotra D.r D. ALFIO» and «Consoli D.na Antonina», who name a Salvatore in November 1846 and again in January 1848. WHAT THIS LEAVES, STATED PLAINLY. Giovanni Nicotra's own marriage certificate says «NATO A GIARRE». Giarre's own registers, read end to end for eleven years, do not hold him. THREE READINGS SURVIVE AND NONE IS PROVED. (1) BOTH HIS DECLARED AGES ARE WRONG and he was born outside 1838-1848 -- he is «trentuno» in 1872 and «ventotto» in 1875, already six years apart, so a third error is not a stretch; the window either side is 1833-1837 and 1849-1853. (2) HE WAS BORN IN GIARRE'S TERRITORY BUT REGISTERED ELSEWHERE. RIPOSTO WAS PART OF GIARRE AND SEPARATED FROM IT IN THIS EXACT PERIOD; a man born in the lower town could call himself «nato a Giarre» and be entered in Riposto's register. THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS FROM GENERAL HISTORY, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT, and the way to test it is to list Riposto on Antenati and read its N sections. (3) «Nato a Giarre» is loose for one of the frazioni -- Macchia, Trepunti, Altarello, San Giovanni Montebello. THE REACH, STATED: this is Giarre's own birth register, every surviving year 1838-1848, read at the only section that could hold the surname, main run AND appendix, in a table that names both parents. It answers for the comune of Giarre and for nothing else.

source: Antenati — RIPOSTO attempted, and the control caught a throttle pretending to be a zero
scope: The Giarre sweep finished clean across eleven years, so Giovanni Nicotra's «nato a Giarre» needs another register. RIPOSTO was part of Giarre and separated from it in this period, so a man from the lower town could say «nato a Giarre» and be entered at Riposto. First step: list Riposto with ?localita=Riposto&s_size=500.
result: NOTHING WAS LEARNED ABOUT RIPOSTO, AND THAT IS THE ENTRY. The query returned ZERO ARKS, NO FACETS and -- the tell -- NO «Nessun risultato trovato» EITHER. A genuine Antenati zero says so in prose; this said nothing at all. THE CONTROL SETTLED IT IN ONE FETCH: the same query shape run against MASCALI, which this archive listed three hours earlier at 498 volumes, came back IDENTICAL -- 520 bytes, title «403 Forbidden». THE SESSION IS RATE-LIMITED, and «Riposto returns nothing» would have been a fact about the throttle. This is the archive's own 520-byte signature, and it is the third distinct shape of false zero met today: the name index whose zero is prose and not a count; the listing that sits at the s_size ceiling and looks complete; and now a 403 that parses as an empty result set. ALL THREE RENDER AS «no results». RIPOSTO IS UNTESTED. Not negative, not a wall -- untested, pending the throttle clearing (this archive's own note gives it twenty minutes or more).

source: Antenati — the false-zero test the Lerena archive asked for, run four ways
scope: The Lerena archive withdrew its own advice: it had told this archive that confirming the POSITIVE assertion of emptiness was the reliable discriminator, and then FamilySearch printed «Historical Record Search Results (0)» and «No Results Found» for every query for an afternoon because its session had expired -- stably, across two reads, after a ninety-second wait, with a control that had passed that morning. Its sharper rules: a control must be RECENT and ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO BE ZERO; ask a SECOND search path on the same source; and when a null looks like a discovery, suspect it hardest. It asked whether the «Nessun risultato trovato» check holds for Antenati in the signed-out state, because that is the state in which the check has to work. FOUR PROBES, ONE MINUTE APART.
result: THE CHECK HOLDS FOR ANTENATI, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL: THERE IS NO SESSION TO EXPIRE. (1) ARITHMETICALLY-IMPOSSIBLE CONTROL: localita=Catania returns «25476 risultati» and 500 arks. A provincial capital cannot be zero, and it was not. (2) TRUE-ZERO SIGNATURE, established deliberately rather than assumed: localita=Zzqqxxwv -- a locality that cannot exist -- returns HTTP 200, a 266 KB page, ZERO arks and «Nessun risultato trovato» in prose. That is what an Antenati nil looks like. (3) THE THROTTLE SIGNATURE, already known and confirmed again: 520 bytes, title «403 Forbidden», no arks, NO «Nessun risultato» -- which is exactly how the Riposto query failed earlier today. The two are distinguishable by SIZE ALONE, 266 KB against 520 bytes. (4) SIGNED-OUT: the same Riposto query run with credentials OMITTED returns byte-identical output to the signed-in one -- 421 risultati, 421 arks. ANTENATI'S REGISTER SEARCH IS PUBLIC AND STATELESS, so there is no cookie to lose and no signed-out state that differs. The Lerena failure mode cannot occur here. WHAT THIS ARCHIVE ADOPTS ANYWAY: the arithmetic control. Every nil re-tested today was controlled against «Arena at Scilla» or «Mascali», both of which merely OUGHT to return something. «Catania» cannot be zero, and that is a stronger guard for nothing extra.

source: Antenati — RIPOSTO opened: 421 volumes, and the ordinary Nicotra live there
scope: Row 177. Giovanni Nicotra's 1872 publication certificate says «nato a GIARRE», and eleven Giarre birth years read end to end -- main runs and appendices -- do not hold him. RIPOSTO registers separately from Giarre from 1821, through the whole window, so a man of the lower town could say Giarre and be entered here. The listing was attempted this morning and returned a throttle; retried after it cleared, with an arithmetically-impossible control alongside.
result: 421 VOLUMES, FACET TOTAL 421, COMPLETE IN ONE PAGE -- comfortably under the s_size ceiling, no paging needed. Banked whole in data/riposto-arks.tsv: 77 Nati, 71 Morti, 69 Matrimoni, 20 Matrimoni processetti, restaurazione 1821-1860 and italiano 1866-1893 WITH A GAP AT 1861-1865 between them. THREE YEARS READ AT THE N SECTION SO FAR. 1841 (his «trentuno in 1872» year): the alphabet runs M straight into P, NO N SECTION -- but the last leaf is TORN, its right page lost, so an appendix cannot be excluded and this is not a finished negative. 1842: M runs into P, NO N SECTION. 1847 (his «ventotto in 1875» year): THE N SECTION HOLDS TWO ENTRIES AND BOTH ARE NICOTRA -- «154. Nicotra Rosa, Riposto, NICOTRA GIUSEPPE / Autieri Angela, 17 Nov 1847» and «152. Nicotra Rosa, do, NICOTRA SALVADORE / Barbagallo Maria, 15 do». NEITHER FATHER IS A ROSARIO, so Giovanni is not among them. BUT THE FINDING IS THE HOUSEHOLDS THEMSELVES. Giarre's only Nicotra in ELEVEN YEARS is a «Dottor Don» with a «Donna» wife -- gentry, and not the family of a bracciante. RIPOSTO HOLDS TWO ORDINARY NICOTRA HOUSEHOLDS IN A SINGLE YEAR. That is where people of Rosario Nicotra's condition carrying his surname actually lived, and it materially raises the odds that his household is in this register in a year not yet read. STILL TO READ: 1838, 1839, 1840, 1843, 1844, 1845, 1846, 1848 and outward, plus the torn tail of 1841. Containers banked for 1840, 1841, 1842, 1846, 1847, 1848. AND ONE NAME NOTED AND NOT CLAIMED: Riposto Nati 1842 entry 11 is «MAZZA FILIPPA», of Mazza Salvadore and Le Greci Grazia. A Mazza household at Riposto. This archive's Mazza are Piedimonte people and nothing connects them; it is recorded because the surname is the archive's own and a reader will ask.

source: An audit of whether the SITE has kept up with the research — and one place it had not
scope: David asked whether the pages, trees and sources were keeping up with two days of fast research -- Mascali, Giarre and Riposto opened, four new people at generation six, Maria Nicotra's birth act found. This archive has twice published a page that had gone stale in the worst direction, so the question was answered by checking rather than by assurance: every page source swept for hard-coded counts and for phrases like «three towns»; the BUILT site searched for each new name; and the person page of the woman at the centre of it read end to end.
result: THE DATA-DRIVEN PAGES WERE ALREADY CURRENT AND THE HAND-WRITTEN ONES MOSTLY WERE. /searched/ carries all 233 rows and reads «2601 volumes across 7 comuni», with Riposto in the holdings table; /corrections/, /worklist/, /method/, /sources/ and /open-questions/ all current; /tree/ draws the new generation six through documented-parents.json. The new names appear across /lines/, /mazza/, /the-name-line/, /what-changed/ and /register/. AND ONE FALSE ALARM OF MY OWN, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY: I reported Maria Nicotra's birth date ABSENT from her own page. It is there in full. My grep was CASE-SENSITIVE and the correction is written in capitals. A tool that judges evidence is evidence, and mine was wrong before the page was. THE REAL GAP, AND IT HAD ONE ROOT: everything keyed on the EXPORT's people could not see the 114 documented additions -- the best-evidenced people in the archive, every one added from a register opened here. No person page, and no marker on the Atlas, which is why ZAMBRONE -- a comune with a read register run and a recorded gap in its deaths -- had no dot at all. Fixed today as row 176. TWO SMALLER THINGS FIXED. The Sicilian narrative page mentioned Mascali and Giarre in passing as neighbouring towns and said nothing of Riposto; it now carries a section saying plainly that THE SICILIAN QUARTER IS FOUR TOWNS, NOT ONE, with what each one holds and what is still missing from it. And a person page's «What is recorded» block is the TREE's account, with any correction further down -- a reader who skims stopped at the wrong town. It now says so and links to it. IT DOES NOT SAY WHICH LINE IS DISPUTED, because corrections.tsv carries prose and not a field name, and inferring which fact a paragraph is about is the kind of guess this archive refuses.

source: Antenati — Riposto births: seven years read, THREE Nicotra households, and none of them Rosario's
scope: Row 177. Giovanni Nicotra's certificate says «nato a GIARRE» and eleven Giarre years do not hold him; RIPOSTO registers separately from Giarre from 1821 and is the only other candidate. Its Tavola is alphabetical and NAMES BOTH PARENTS. Seven years now read at the N section, each checked into the next letter.
result: SEVEN YEARS, THREE NICOTRA HOUSEHOLDS, AND ROSARIO IS IN NONE OF THEM. 1838: one entry, «170. NICOTRA MARIA», father FRANCESCO. 1840: the alphabet runs M straight into P, NO N SECTION. 1841: likewise no N section -- and its last leaf is TORN, so that year is not a finished negative. 1842: no N section. 1846: the N heading is WRITTEN AND LEFT EMPTY, and so is the O beneath it. 1847: TWO entries, both Nicotra -- «154. Nicotra Rosa, NICOTRA GIUSEPPE / Autieri Angela, 17 Nov» and «152. Nicotra Rosa, NICOTRA SALVADORE / Barbagallo Maria, 15 do». 1848: one entry, «166. NICOTRA LEONARDO, Riposto, Nicotra Giuseppe / Autieri Angela, 26 Dicembre» -- the same household as the year before. SO RIPOSTO HOLDS AT LEAST THREE ORDINARY NICOTRA HOUSEHOLDS in the window: GIUSEPPE x ANGELA AUTIERI (1847 and 1848), SALVADORE x MARIA BARBAGALLO (1847), and FRANCESCO (1838). THAT IS THE POINT OF THE TOWN. Giarre's only Nicotra across ELEVEN years is a «Dottor Don» with a «Donna» wife; Mascali's only one across nine years is an Alfio. Riposto has three in seven, all of them the sort of family a bracciante marries into -- and still not the one this archive wants. STILL UNREAD: 1839, 1843, 1844 and 1845, and the torn tail of 1841. Their containers could not be fetched: the origin returned the 520-byte «403 Forbidden» signature four times across two attempts, which is the throttle and not a result. THE IMAGES ARE NEVER THROTTLED, only the HTML that carries a container id -- so this is a wait, not a wall. AND ONE ROUTE NOT YET TRIED THAT MAY NOT NEED THEM: Riposto's 1841 births exist in a SECOND VOLUME, «17517, suppl. 2» (an_ua73235), which may carry the leaf the first volume has lost.

source: Antenati — RIPOSTO Matrimoni 1835–1846 and the remaining Nati: twelve marriage years and the torn 1841 tail
scope: The Riposto birth sweep had left 1844 and 1845 unread and 1841 unfinished (torn last leaf). And the better instrument had never been opened: the restauration marriage Tavola names BOTH SPOUSES, ALL FOUR PARENTS and the comune each spouse came from, so Rosario Nicotra × Venera Murabito's own marriage would hand over generation seven in a single row.
result: ROSARIO IS IN NONE OF THE TWELVE MARRIAGE YEARS, AND THE BIRTH SWEEP IS NOW COMPLETE FOR ELEVEN YEARS. THE FIND IS RIPOSTO MATRIMONI 1844 ATTO 39: «NICOTRA SALVADORE», PATRIA GIARRE, son of NICOTRA ALFIO and PAPPALARDO ROSA, marrying Barbagallo Maria of Riposto, daughter of Rosario Barbagallo and Anna Campagna, in July 1844 (the day is not legible in the index). HE IS THE FATHER OF THE TWO RIPOSTO CHILDREN THE BIRTH SWEEP ALREADY HELD — Nicotra Alfio, atto 75, 9 May 1845, and Nicotra Rosa, 15 November 1847. HE IS NOT GIOVANNI'S FATHER. What he settles is the argument behind the whole search: «nato a Giarre» and «absent from Giarre's registers» stopped being a contradiction the moment a second man did both. THE BIRTH YEARS FINISHED: 1844 has the N heading WRITTEN AND LEFT BLANK, the facing page opening at O. 1845 has ONE N entry, Nicotra Alfio of Salvadore and Maria Barbagallo. AND 1841 IS CLOSED: the first volume's alphabet runs M into P with its last leaf torn and the right page lost, but THE SECOND 1841 VOLUME (17517 suppl. 2) CARRIES ITS OWN UNTORN TAVOLA, and there M runs into O with NO N HEADING AT ALL — and the O it holds, Oliveri Francesco atto 93, is exactly what the torn leaf lost. A DUPLICATE IS A COPY AND NOT A SECOND WITNESS, and that is said on the page too; what it gives is reach, not corroboration. THE REACH: Riposto's own registers, births 1838–1848 and marriages 1835–1846, at the only section that could hold the surname. They answer for Riposto and for nothing else.

source: Antenati — MASCALI Matrimoni 1835–1847, and the caution that cost the birth sweep its certainty
scope: Rosario Nicotra was «di Mascali» in the 1872 act, so if he married in his own comune his marriage is here. Eight years were openable. Each was read from the first section heading to «Fine» rather than at the M-to-next-letter junction.
result: NO NICOTRA IN ANY OF THE EIGHT YEARS. The only N entries are NICOLOSI Francesco × Mercurio Francesca (1840 atto 10) and NERI Leonardo × Borzì Maria (1847 atto 8), and the 1847 entry is the important one FOR A REASON THAT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH THE NAME. ITS N SECTION SITS BEFORE THE M. This clerk's headings run C, then N, then M. 1841 and 1835 put V before S. THE SECTIONS AT MASCALI ARE NOT IN ALPHABETICAL ORDER, which means «the alphabet runs M straight into P, therefore there is no N» PROVES NOTHING HERE. The eight marriage years above were read whole and stand. THE NINE MASCALI BIRTH YEARS OF 1839–1848 WERE READ AT THE JUNCTION, BEFORE THIS WAS KNOWN, AND ARE NOW MARKED PROVISIONAL — on the Mascali page and on the work list, row 180. Nothing FOUND is withdrawn: Alfio Nicotra and Carmela Sudieri are still in 1840 and 1847. Only the NEGATIVES are weaker than they were written, and saying so is cheaper than discovering it later.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Nati 1820, the first year Sicily registered anything
scope: Riposto Matrimoni 1844 put Nicotra Salvadore's birth at Giarre about 1815–1824 — a decade earlier than the eleven Giarre years already read. Sicilian civil registration begins in 1820 and there is nothing before it, so 1820 is the floor. Its N section was read whole, at full width.
result: TWO UNTITLED NICOTRA HOUSEHOLDS IN THE FIRST VOLUME. Atto 198, Nicotra Rosaria, of NICOTRA SIMONE and Marianna Dadone, 13 April. Atto 228, Nicotra Carmela, of NICOTRA ROSARIO and Rosa Providenza, 1 May. No Don, no Donna, written the way a labourer's name is written. SO «GIARRE'S ONLY NICOTRA IS A DOTTOR DON» WAS NEVER A FACT ABOUT GIARRE — IT WAS A FACT ABOUT ELEVEN YEARS OF IT, and this archive had let the eleven stand for the town. THE SECOND FATHER IS CALLED ROSARIO AND IT IS NOT HIM: Giovanni's father was a working bracciante in October 1872 and a man fathering a child in May 1820 would be past seventy-five by then. It is the generation a grandson is named after, which is naming custom, which this archive already files as weak evidence. THE NAME IS RECORDED AND THE JOIN IS NOT MADE. The test is Salvadore Nicotra's own birth act, which would say whether Alfio, Simone and Rosario are brothers. Also in the same section and not Nicotra: Nicolosi Pietro, Nota Alessandro, Nucifora Alfio.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1835–1846 and Nati 1821–1826: blocked by the rate limiter, not by the register
scope: The obvious next sweeps after Giarre 1820: the remaining early birth years, which would hold Salvadore Nicotra's own act, and the Giarre marriage Tavole, where Rosario Nicotra × Venera Murabito would be if he married in the town his son was born in.
result: NOT A NEGATIVE AND NOT A WALL — UNREAD. Twenty-one ark→container lookups were attempted and ONE returned before the throttle took the rest: every other one came back with this archive's known 520-byte, HTTP 403, «no Nessun risultato» signature. CORRECTED FROM YESTERDAY'S NOTE: a three-second pause between lookups does NOT keep you under the limiter, it only raises the batch from two or three to about twenty-eight. THE LIMITER IS CUMULATIVE. And a fifteen-minute wait after a lock was NOT enough — exactly one fetch got through before it closed again, so recovery is gradual rather than a clean reset. THE IMAGES THEMSELVES ARE NEVER THROTTLED; it is only the HTML page that carries a container id. So this is a queue to work through at about twenty-five containers a session, not a problem with Giarre.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1844, and the Don Alfio who is «of S. Giovanni» in one register and «of Giarre» in another
scope: The Giarre marriage containers came through after the throttle cleared. 1844 was opened first because that is the year Nicotra Salvadore married at Riposto, and a brother marrying at home would sit beside him. The N section was read at full width.
result: TWO N ENTRIES AND THE IMPORTANT ONE IS NOT ROSARIO. Atto 54, 19 August 1844: NICOTRA D.r D. ALFIO, PATRIA GIARRE, son of Nicotra D. Giuseppe and CALTABIANO D. GIOACHINA, marrying Consoli D. Antonina — the couple whose Salvatore appears in the birth index in November 1846 and again in January 1848. Also atto 8, Noscia Mro Ignazio × Castorina Anna, which is not a Nicotra. THE FINDING IS A JOIN THIS ARCHIVE HAD REFUSED TO MAKE. Riposto Matrimoni 1838 atto 15 marries «Nicotra D. Alfio, son of FU D. GIUSEPPE and D. GIOACHINA CATTABIANO» to Ligresti D. Angela. THE SAME TWO PARENTS. It is ONE MAN, widowed and remarried across two comuni, and the household file said in September that whether he was Giarre's Don Alfio remarried «is not decided here». It is decided now, by the parents and not by the name. AND THE TWO REGISTERS GIVE HIM TWO BIRTHPLACES: Riposto wrote his patria «S. GIOVANNI», Giarre wrote «GIARRE». SAN GIOVANNI MONTEBELLO IS A FRAZIONE OF GIARRE, so both are true. THAT IS THE THIRD READING OF GIOVANNI NICOTRA'S PROBLEM, DOCUMENTED IN HIS OWN SURNAME: a man of this district can be «nato a Giarre» in one register and entered under a frazione's name in another. It does not find Giovanni; it makes his case possible without either of his declared ages being wrong. STILL TO READ: Giarre Matrimoni 1835-1843 and 1845-1846, containers banked. THE REACH: one year of one comune's marriage index, at the only section that could hold the surname.

source: Antenati — the MASCALI riveli of 1616 opened: the oldest source in this archive, and it has a name index
scope: Forty-six Mascali volumes sit at PALERMO rather than Catania and are not civil registration at all: they are RIVELI DI BENI E DI ANIME, household returns made to the Sicilian parliament, and the earliest is 1616 — two centuries before any register this archive has read and the oldest source of any kind in it. The first volume was opened to find out what it is.
result: 546 IMAGES, AND IT OPENS WITH AN ALPHABETICAL NAME INDEX, WITH THE LETTER TABS CUT INTO THE FORE-EDGE OF THE BOOK — B C D E F G I L M N P R S T V are visible in the photograph, AND THERE IS AN N. Each line gives a name and a folio number. THE CATCH, AND IT DECIDES HOW THIS IS SEARCHED: THE INDEX IS ORDERED BY FORENAME, NOT BY SURNAME. The A pages run Antonino lo Xuto, Antonino Puliseva, Antonio Barbagallo, Antonino Gagliano, Adamo Mangano, Alfonso di Lonardo, Aloisia lo Castro, Agata Grasso, Alfio Pinnisi, Alfio Musumeci, Antonino Musumeci and so on. So the N tab leads to Natale and Nicolo, NOT to Nicotra, and finding a surname means reading the index through rather than jumping to a letter. That is still perhaps twenty images instead of five hundred and forty-six, which is the difference between a task and a wall. THE SURNAMES ARE THE SAME ONES THE 1840s REGISTERS ARE FULL OF — Barbagallo, Musumeci, Finocchiaro, Grasso, Gagliano, Pinnisi, Strano, Arcidiacono, Puliseo — which says the population is continuous across two hundred years even though no line of descent is drawn. NO NICOTRA SEEN YET AND NONE LOOKED FOR PROPERLY: one opening of the index was read. THE REACH: this says what the instrument is and nothing about who is in it.

source: Trove API v3 — the naturalisation gazettes, swept by surname now that a key exists
scope: David obtained a Trove API key on 27 September, valid to December 2026, which closes work-list row 153 and unblocks rows 7 and 79. Row 79 had failed on the TOOL and not the source: Trove's search page accepts a query, echoes it back, throws inside its own vendor bundle on a storage API the browser pane does not provide, and never paints a result list. The API needs no JavaScript. Seven surnames swept in the newspaper category, which includes the Commonwealth of Australia Gazette.
result: SEVEN NATURALISATION ENTRIES, IN A SOURCE THAT HAD BEEN BLOCKED FOR EIGHT DAYS. PROSTAMO: Angela and Antonino Giacomo, gazetted 16 November 1961; Assunta, 3 November 1966. POLISTENA: Maria Luisa, 22 January 1959; Maria, 13 March 1969; Annunziato, 20 March 1969. MELLUSO: Francesco, 6 July 1961. ALL ARE CANDIDATES AND NONE IS A JOIN — data/trove-gazette.tsv says so row by row. A certificate-of-naturalisation notice in this gazette is a NAME IN AN ALPHABETICAL LIST and nothing else: no birth date, no address, no former nationality in these notices, so there is nothing in them to disambiguate two men of one name with. ANGELA PROSTAMO IS THE ONE NEW NAME; the rest match people the export already holds. AND ONE DISCREPANCY WORTH KEEPING: this archive already held «Maria Assunta's gazettal of 4 JULY 1966»; the notice found here is 3 NOVEMBER 1966 and prints ASSUNTA without the Maria. Two notices or two readings, and which has not been established. TWO THINGS THE API WILL NOT DO, both of which look like absence. (1) IT DOES NOT SERVE ARTICLE TEXT FOR GOVERNMENT GAZETTE NOTICES: `include=articletext` is accepted and silently ignored on /result AND on /newspaper/<id>, and `snippet` comes back empty, which reads exactly like an article with no words in it. The OCR is on the public page at nla.gov.au/nla.news-article<id> and tools/trove.py fetches it there. (2) THE DEFAULT SEARCH IS NOT EXACT: «Anile» returns 5,834,914 results — it is matching inside longer words, which is this estate's own «short token inside a long word» trap arriving in a new source, and that surname needs a phrase query before any of it means anything. THE OCR IS ALSO TWO COLUMNS READ ACROSS: entries print «Surname, Given Names» and flatten into «Prineas, Panagiotis Prostamo, Angela Prostamo, Antonmo Giacomo Przybylo, Jozef», so the given name after a surname belongs with THAT surname and «Antonmo» is Antonino. THE REACH: seven surnames, the newspaper and gazette category, certificate-of-naturalization notices only. Trove's newspapers largely stop at 1955 and the gazette runs to 1973, so this answers for the naturalisation window and for nothing later. THE 1942 INTERNMENTS (row 7) ARE NOT YET SWEPT.

source: Trove API — the 1942 internments: two named internees, and the newspapers do not name them
scope: Work-list row 7, unblocked the same day as the API key. The NAA has already given two named internees in this family — ROSARIO MAZZA (MP1103/1 Q8110, born 20 February 1899) and MARIO CRUPI, both held at LOVEDAY in South Australia from 18 August 1942 to 30 December 1943. The row's hope was that «internees' names sometimes printed». Four phrase queries: each man by name, Loveday with internment, and Mazza against internee and Queensland.
result: THE NEWSPAPERS DO NOT NAME EITHER MAN AS AN INTERNEE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. «Rosario Mazza» returns FOURTEEN articles, every one of them Queensland and none of them about internment: a wine overcharging fine at Brisbane in March 1947, a warning on dirty premises in September 1947, an eviction case in 1952, a Gordonvale police court in 1935. THEY MAY WELL BE HIS — he was released in December 1943 and a Brisbane tradesman in the late forties fits — but a name in a court report is not an identification and none of them is attached. «Mario Crupi» returns SIX, all in the right country: Innisfail, Cairns, Tully, Townsville, which is exactly where this archive already places the Crupi brothers. None mentions internment either. WHAT TROVE DOES HOLD IS THE CAMP, NOT THE ROLL. «Loveday» with internment returns 1,085 articles and they are good ones — «ITALIAN INTERNEES AT LOVEDAY: First Train Load Arrives», Murray Pioneer, 12 June 1941; preparations at the camp in May 1941; the Italians leaving in 1948. The South Australian papers covered the camp's existence closely and its inmates anonymously. SO THE ROW'S PREMISE IS TESTED AND FALSE FOR THESE TWO MEN. Internee names were not routinely printed, and the NAA file remains the only place either man is named. THE REACH: Trove's digitised newspapers, four phrase queries, both men by full name. Trove's newspaper run largely ends in 1954, which COVERS the 1942–43 internment window completely — this is not a coverage gap, it is an absence in the source.

source: Trove — every Australian person this archive holds, searched by name, and where the source ends
scope: Asked whether Trove has anything left. Rather than guess: every Mazza this archive places in Australia searched by full name, plus the nine other surnames, plus the remaining naturalisation sweep. Phrase form `text:"..."`, established below.
result: SIXTEEN QUEENSLAND HITS ACROSS EVERY AUSTRALIAN MAZZA THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS, and most of the names return NOTHING: Michele, Ignazio, Venera Mazza, Alfonso Prostamo, Caterina Melluso, Giovanni Polistena are all zero. TWO ARE WORTH HAVING AND BOTH ARE BEHIND A WALL. (1) SEBASTIANO MAZZA, News-Mail (Bundaberg), 6 JULY 1962, headed «THREE NEW CITIZENS», snippet «Supported by friends and relatives, three former Italian citizens received certificates of...» — A NATURALISATION CEREMONY REPORT. (2) SEBASTIANO MAZZA again, same paper, 28 SEPTEMBER 1963, «Family Notices». Also CONCETTA MAZZA, a Queensland «Family Notices» of 17 FEBRUARY 1958. ALL THREE CARRY `status: currently unavailable`. Trove indexes these post-1955 Queensland papers and will not serve the text — the article pages 404 at both nla.gov.au/nla.news-article<id> and trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/<id>, though the search matched inside them. THIS IS A COPYRIGHT WALL, NOT AN ABSENCE, and the distinction matters: the words exist, are indexed, and are reachable another way. About 13 per cent of Nicotra hits carry the same flag. AND THE 1962 CEREMONY CONTRADICTS SOMETHING THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS. Row 105 reasons that Sebastiano Mazza was naturalised BEFORE 1959, because only British subjects could be enrolled and he is on the 1959 Queensland roll at Wacol. A naturalisation ceremony at BUNDABERG in July 1962 does not fit that, and Bundaberg is three hundred and fifty kilometres from Wacol. Either it is a different Sebastiano Mazza, or one of the two readings is wrong. NOT RESOLVED HERE and not attached to him. THE PHRASE FORM, because the obvious one does not work: `"Anile"` in quotes returns 5,834,914 — IDENTICAL to the unquoted total, so quoting does not bind. `text:"Anile"` returns 41,162, a 99.3 per cent cut. Controls run alongside: `Zzqqxxwv` returns 0 quoted and unquoted, so a zero here is real, and `Catania` returns 30,090. THE REACH: Trove's digitised newspapers and the Commonwealth Gazette, every Australian person in this archive by full name. It does NOT answer for anyone who never reached Australia, and it does not answer for the post-1955 Queensland press, which it indexes and withholds.

source: Trove — the categories that are not newspapers, and the Queensland wills hiding in them
scope: Asked a second time whether Trove was finished, and the honest answer was that I had only searched ONE OF ITS CATEGORIES. Rows 7, 79 and 153 are all about newspapers and the Commonwealth Gazette; Trove also aggregates books, images, magazines, music, people, research and «diaries, letters and archives», the last of which carries ITEM-LEVEL RECORDS FROM STATE ARCHIVES. Eleven surnames across eight categories, with the Zzqqxxwv control run in every one of them.
result: TROVE IS NOT FINISHED, AND THE THING IT WAS HIDING IS BETTER THAN ANYTHING IN THE NEWSPAPERS. The `diary` category surfaces QUEENSLAND STATE ARCHIVES item records, and four of them are NICOTRA WILLS: SALVATORE PHILIP (1955, ITM938108), LEONARDA (1962), VINCENZO (1965), FILIPPO (1966) — all «Part of series Supreme Court (Northern) Ecclesiastical Files (Wills) (S6220)», all held at QSA, all marked OPEN ACCESS. A will file names the deceased, the date of death, the address, the occupation, the executors and the beneficiaries, which is usually the whole household. ALL FOUR ARE TOWNSVILLE DISTRICT, AND NORTH QUEENSLAND HAS ALREADY COME UP TWICE IN THIS SWEEP: the only two Nicotra family notices in the newspapers are the Evening Advocate (INNISFAIL), 1 May and 17 September 1953, and the Lands Department holds three Nicotra land files for Innisfail and Cardwell Shire. THERE IS A NORTH QUEENSLAND NICOTRA CLUSTER and this archive has never looked at it. WHETHER IT IS MARIA NICOTRA'S FAMILY IS COMPLETELY UNKNOWN — she died at Brisbane in 1963, four hundred kilometres south — and nothing here is attached to anybody. ALSO FOUND: «Naturalisation - Central District - MAZZA, James, 1898» at Rockhampton, half a century before this family reached Australia and recorded so nobody chases it twice. And court files under CASSANITI and MURABITO — both surnames off the Nicotra line — but dated 2014, 2015 and 2018, which is modern and touches the living, so they are named here and not pursued. AND A CORRECTION TO THE SAME DAY'S WORK. This archive was told a few hours earlier that Trove could be closed. THAT ADVICE WAS WRONG, and wrong in a way worth writing down: the sweep was thorough inside one category and never asked what the other seven held. A source is not exhausted because the part of it you know about is. THE REACH: eight Trove categories, eleven surnames, controls in each. It does not reach anyone who never came to Australia.

source: Antenati — Giarre Nati 1827 and 1828, the annual Tavole read whole
scope: Giarre (Catania), Stato civile della restaurazione. 1827: ark an_ua68985, segnatura 15927, container 5xe4lba, 175 images, Tavola at folios 170-173. 1828: ark an_ua68986, segnatura 15928, container wRGJ3ja, 237 images, Tavola at folios 229-230. Archivio di Stato di Catania. Both Tavole read from the first heading to the last rather than by junction, because a junction negative is unsafe where section order cannot be assumed.
result: A NULL ON NICOTRA IN BOTH. The N heading is ruled and left blank in each year, with O blank beneath it, then P opens at Pafumi act 34 (1827) and Pennisi act 12 (1828). The first MURABITO households this archive has found anywhere turned up instead — three of them across the two years, one of which names a daughter Venera in 1827 and another daughter in 1828. Murabito is a common Giarre surname, so «Venera Murabito of Giarre» is ordinary rather than remarkable. The 1827 Venera is NOT Rosario Nicotra's wife: born 1827 she would have been fourteen when Giovanni was born about 1841.

source: Antenati — Mascali, whether a 1844 volume exists in any series
scope: Mascali (Catania), the whole holding: 498 results, 498 distinct arks, facet totals agreeing, so a complete listing and not a sample at the page-size ceiling. Every series checked for 1844 — Nati, Morti, Matrimoni, Nati esposti, Matrimoni processetti, the memorandum notificazioni, and Diversi.
result: MASCALI HAS NO 1844 IN ANY RESTAURAZIONE SERIES. The run goes 1843 then 1845 throughout, and both counters step by exactly one across the gap — ark an_ua70313 to an_ua70314, Catania segnatura 16777 to 16778 — where every other year steps by one per year. The year was never deposited rather than dropped from a listing. GIARRE HAS 1844, so this is Mascali's hole and not a regional one. Any Mascali negative spanning 1844 is complete without it, and no search should be planned for it.

source: Antenati — which endpoints the rate limiter actually governs
scope: Tested across a working day while the site was refusing traffic: the ark landing pages (antenati.cultura.gov.it/ark:/12657/...), the search listing (/ricerca/), the IIIF image service (iiif-antenati.cultura.gov.it) and the container manifest (dam-antenati.cultura.gov.it/antenati/containers/<id>/manifest).
result: THE THROTTLE IS ON THE HTML, NOT ON THE IMAGES. Ark pages and /ricerca/ returned a blanket 403 all day, including to an ordinary browser, while the IIIF image service and the container manifest served every request without complaint. So a volume whose CONTAINER is already recorded can be read in full during a throttle; only the ark-to-container lookup is blocked. That is the argument for banking container ids in the ark tables as they are found. Also: asking IIIF for a width greater than the image's own returns a 403 whose BODY IS AN HTML ERROR PAGE, which will be saved as a .jpg by anything that does not check.

source: Antenati — Mascali Morti 1882, and the early M of 1881
scope: Mascali (Catania), Stato civile italiano. 1882: ark an_ua81729, segnatura 8853, container 0JbrlJG, 53 images, Indice Annuale at folio 40. 1881: ark an_ua81728, segnatura 8852, container LPR9gW8, 63 images, index at folio 38. Both indexes read whole, M and N, across the paired exposures described in the row below.
result: BOTH NULL ON NICOTRA'S ROSARIO AND ON MURABITO. 1882 holds three N entries — Neri Maria 75, Nucifora Filippo 82, Nicolosi Enna 106 — and no Murabito in M. 1881 holds five — Nicotra Nunziato 2, Nicotra Salvatore 14, Neri Salvatore 16, Neri Maria 37, Nucifora Maria 61 — and its EARLY M, previously unread behind the card, holds no Murabito either. That matters because an Italian death index files a married woman under her maiden surname, so the M section is where a Venera Murabito would appear and half of 1881's had never been looked at. 1882 had been recorded as unreadable and was not.

source: Antenati — the DUPLICATA card is moved between exposures, so a covered page is not a lost one
scope: Observed in two Mascali death volumes at the Archivio di Stato di Catania, containers 0JbrlJG (1882, images 51 and 52) and LPR9gW8 (1881, images 61 and 62). Method note, not a family finding.
result: WHERE A BLACK «DUPLICATA» CARD COVERS HALF AN OPENING, LOOK AT THE ADJACENT IMAGE. The opening is photographed TWICE and the card is moved between exposures — once resting on the left-hand page, once on the right — so the two images together give every column. The card identifies the archive's duplicate copy; it is not damage and it is not a redaction. A session that reads one image and stops will record a year as unreadable when it is fully legible, and that is exactly what happened here: Mascali Morti 1882 sat as «hidden behind the cover sheet» for a day, and 1881 had half its M section written off the same way. Neither volume has a second copy to fall back on, so the mistake would have been permanent. Separately: the volume's back cover may carry the archive's own condition labels — PAG. ONDULATE, PAG. MACCHIATA, PAG. TRASPARENTE, TUTTO IL VOLUME, IMPOSSIBILE FARE DI MEGLIO — which describe the paper and say nothing about whether the index can be read.

source: Antenati — Mascali Nati 1873, 1874, 1876 and 1877, the annual indexes and two acts
scope: Mascali (Catania), Stato civile italiano, Archivio di Stato di Catania. 1873 ark an_ua81752 segn 8759 container wE72Q9W (70 images, index folio 56, act 145 at image 60); 1874 an_ua81753 / 8760 / w68j9AQ (70, folio 63); 1876 an_ua81755 / 8762 / 5gKnx4N (85, folio 70); 1877 an_ua81756 / 8763 / LpAxl61 (78, folio 66, act 8 at image 6). N section read whole in each year; two acts fetched in full. 1873 and 1874 carry a PATERNITÀ column in the index and 1876 and 1877 do not, which decides whether a father can be had without fetching the act.
result: THE TARGET HOUSEHOLD FOUND, AND TWO MORE BESIDE IT. Mascali Nati 1873 atto 145 is the birth of VENERA NICOTRA to GIOVANNI NICOTRA DI ROSARIO, lavorante, and VENERA CASSANITI FU GAETANO, at contrada Nocille — «di» Rosario and not «fu», in an act that writes «fu» for the wife's dead father four lines below, so the father was alive in December 1873. 1874, 1876 and 1877 hold no further child of that couple, which fits the two births already known. Three other Nicotra households at Mascali: GAETANO x CARMELA CAVALLARO of Nunziata (daughters 1874 and 1877, the second read in full), GIUSEPPE FU ANGELO (a witness Giovanni chose himself), and an ALFIO fathering a child in 1873. Act 4 of 1877, Nicotra Mariano, remains unread. A namesake worth knowing: TWO Maria Nicotras born at Mascali twenty months apart, 1874 to Gaetano and 1875 to Giovanni.

source: Antenati — Giarre Nati 1827-1837, closing the 1820-1848 run
scope: Giarre (Catania), Stato civile della restaurazione, Archivio di Stato di Catania. Eleven annual Tavole, each read from the first heading to the last rather than by junction — 1834's alphabet runs P, Q, V, S, so junction negatives are unsafe in these volumes. Arks an_ua68985 to an_ua68995, containers 5xe4lba, wRGJ3ja, 5vxY4ly, LpA8n1Z, wQ8J9vY, 5GE26Nx, 5vxY4Kl, Lapd1WA, 5dZj6aK, LqJro1B, wbr2VZX. With the years already held this COMPLETES Giarre births 1820-1848: twenty-nine consecutive years, no gaps.
result: A NULL ON NICOTRA ACROSS THE WHOLE DECADE, and the completed run turns it into a finding. Giarre's ordinary Nicotra appear in 1820 and 1821 — four households, two of them headed by a ROSARIO — and then disappear from the birth registers for twenty-four years, after which the only Nicotra left is a titled «Dottor Don» line in 1846 and 1848. The N section is ruled and blank in six of the eleven years and ABSENT ALTOGETHER in four; the one N entry in 1836 is a Nicciò. GIOVANNI NICOTRA, whose 1872 marriage act says «nato a GIARRE» and whose age puts his birth between about 1841 and about 1847, is in none of it, and neither is a sibling. Either the birth went unregistered, or «Giarre» meant a frazione or the district rather than the comune, or he was born elsewhere. SIX MURABITO HOUSEHOLDS were recorded in passing, three of them against the one name Giuseppe Murabito with three different wives, and TWO daughters called Venera — so Venera Murabito is an ordinary Giarre name and cannot be pinned on the name alone.

source: Antenati — Mascali Morti 1873-1893 swept whole, and Rosario Nicotra found
scope: Mascali (Catania), Stato civile italiano, Archivio di Stato di Catania. All 21 annual death indexes 1873-1893, the whole digitised range. Every index read for MURABITO in the M section as well as NICOTRA in the N, because an Italian death index files a married woman under her MAIDEN surname. Most volumes needed BOTH paired exposures: the archive's black DUPLICATA card covers one page of an opening in one image and the other page in the next.
result: ROSARIO NICOTRA FOUND, atto 35 of 1890, read in the original: «è morto NICOTRA ROSARIO, di anni NOVANTA CIRCA, CONTADINO, residente in Mascali, NATO IN GIARRE, da fu SIMONE, e da fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA, MARITO DI MURABITO VENERA», died 4 April 1890 at contrada Montargi. Born about 1800 AT GIARRE — which is very likely why his son's 1872 marriage act says «nato a Giarre» — with a trade, a death, a wife named beside him and TWO PARENTS the archive did not have, a seventh generation. «MARITO», not «vedovo», so VENERA MURABITO OUTLIVED HIM; she appears in none of these 21 indexes, and 1893 is where Antenati's Mascali stops, so her death is beyond the digitised range and needs the comune or a certificate. Also found: the first MURABITO at Mascali rather than Giarre — BARTOLO, bracciale, born Mascali, son of a Paolo, died 1885 atto 4, declared 106; and SALVATORE Murabito 1886 atto 78. Four other Nicotra households, and two 1883 Nicotra infant deaths proved by their acts to belong to other families.

source: Antenati — Mascali Matrimoni 1835-1847 and Riposto Matrimoni 1830-1846, swept whole
scope: Mascali and Riposto (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. Mascali's thirteen marriage Tavole 1835-1847 (1844 was never deposited) and Riposto's seventeen 1830-1846. MASCALI'S SECTIONS ARE NOT IN ALPHABETICAL ORDER — 1847 runs C, N, M; 1841 and 1835 put V before S — so every volume was read heading by heading and no junction negative was taken.
result: NO NICOTRA GROOM AT MASCALI IN THIRTEEN YEARS; four of its Tavole have no N section at all. Riposto 1830 holds the ONLY Nicotra groom found in any marriage index across three towns and 118 read years: atto 12, «D. FRANCESCO NICOTRA di anni venticinque, NATO IN GIARRE, CALZOLAJO, figlio di D. GIUSEPPE e di ROSARIA MISANO di anni sessantaquattro», marrying Maria Sapienza of Riposto. The «D.» is Don and the trade is artisan, so this is the TITLED Giarre Nicotra and not the bracciante line — but Rosaria Misano born about 1766 makes them the earliest Nicotra generation reached anywhere. NOTE FOR ANYONE USING THESE INDEXES: they list by the GROOM'S surname only, so a bride of the name will not appear under her own letter.

source: Antenati — MASCALI Matrimoni 1820–1829, the decade Rosario would have married in
scope: Mascali (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. All ten marriage Tavole of 1820–1829, each read from its first section heading to its last rather than at the M-to-next-letter junction. Containers w992969, wlG7G22, 57PKPmX, wXrJr7v, w68l8zb, wRGbGWQ, 0A4p4mg, 0Jb9beG, 0Jb9brG, 0ZJeJRa. Every year checked against the register's own closing line, which states the act count in words, so each reading is a whole table and not a half: venticinque, undici, sedici, ventiquattro, trentuno, trentuno, quindici, and the rest.
result: NO NICOTRA GROOM IN ANY OF THE TEN YEARS. Seven have no N heading ruled at all; three carry a single N entry and none is a Nicotra — NICIFORA Leonardo (1824 atto 22), NICIFORA Mariano (1825 atto 17), NICOLOSI Salvadore (1827 atto 10). 1827 IS THE ONE TO REMEMBER: ITS N SECTION SITS AFTER THE P. The headings run C, F, G, M, P, N, R, T, V, so a reader who stopped at the M–P junction would have called the year empty and been wrong. That is the third independent proof that MASCALI'S SECTIONS ARE NOT ALPHABETICAL — 1847 runs C, N, M and 1841 and 1835 put V before S. One find attached to nobody: the 1825 groom's mother is written NICOTRA MARIA, a Nicotra woman born by about 1785, a generation above Rosario; a shared surname in one town is not a link. This closes Mascali as the place Rosario Nicotra married. His 1890 death act says NATO IN GIARRE, and Giarre is where the marriage must now be looked for.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1820–1829, the decade in Rosario's birthplace
scope: Giarre (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. All ten marriage Tavole 1820–1829, each read from its first ruled letter to its last. Containers LqJrKnB, 5VKXP9J, wrdrmWX, 5VKXPmV, LydYKx1, wbr2Ron, wrdrmey, Lme8RKK, LoYEKVR, LeGQRZD. Opened because Rosario Nicotra's 1890 Mascali death act says NATO IN GIARRE and Mascali's own marriage decade had just come back empty.
result: TWO NICOTRA GROOMS IN 1820 — the first found in any Giarre marriage index. ATTO 30, 1 May: NICOTRA SALVADORE x Strano Giuseppa, son of NICOTRA CIRINO and PELLINI MARIA. ATTO 80, 31 July: NICOTRA GIUSEPPE x Cattabiano Rosa, son of NICOTRA MASTRO SEBASTIANO and TORNABENE CARMELA. Neither is Rosario, who was about twenty that year; these are two Nicotra HOUSEHOLDS of Giarre standing in the same generation as his father Simone. The acts themselves are in the same volume and are not yet read. THE OTHER NINE YEARS GIVE NOTHING: 1822 and 1824 hold a single N entry each and both are NICOLOSI, 1821 has no N heading at all, and 1823, 1825, 1826, 1827, 1828 and 1829 have the heading RULED AND BLANK. FOR ANYONE USING THESE INDEXES: Giarre's clerks rule every letter whether or not it carries an entry — 1823 rules A·B, D·E, N, O and Q all empty — so a blank heading at Giarre is a positive statement of absence. That is the opposite of Mascali, whose clerks file out of order and whose silences prove nothing. CAVEAT ON 1820: the Tavola's first leaf (entries 1–56, letters A–L) was never photographed; the index is strictly alphabetical and the N section is bounded by M before and O after, but the year is not a whole reading and is not recorded as one.

source: Antenati — RIPOSTO Matrimoni 1821–1829, the decade completed
scope: Riposto (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. All nine marriage Tavole 1821–1829 — Riposto's civil registers begin in 1821 — each read from its first ruled letter to «Fine». Containers w68qppe, w99mlP6, 5GEmr1N, wrd7kap, wE71q3d, LqJm8qP, wlG6nqY, 5YGADzP, wbrBz3Z. Every year checked against the register's own closing line, which states the act count in words.
result: THE N HEADING IS RULED IN ALL NINE YEARS AND CARRIES NOTHING IN ANY OF THEM. No Nicotra, and no N entry of any surname, in the whole decade.
